title: INDIA bloc passes 'resolution' to 'impeach' CEC Gyanesh Kumar at Kharge's residence - top developments
text: NEW DELHI: The Congress-led INDIA bloc on Saturday unanimously passed a "motion" to "impeach" Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar in a "mock Parliament" held at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge 's residence. The exercise was held amid allegations of irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls under Kumar's watch. Separately, The Indian Express reported last month that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times to decisions they alleged were taken without their knowledge. These included decisions concerning the SIR, adding to the scrutiny of Kumar.The "impeachment" exercise is being held a day ahead of the INDIA bloc's "Delhi Chalo" rally at Ramlila Maidan, where the opposition will seek Kumar's resignation. title: âIf match umpire is biased, what is the point of playing?â Sachin Pilot questions CECâs neutrality
text: Pilot questions CEC's neutrality NEW DELHI: Congress leader Sachin Pilot on Saturday questioned the neutrality of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that his conduct and the process governing his appointment and post-retirement immunity had raised concerns about the independence of the Election Commission. In an interview with news agency ANI, Pilot alleged that the CEC's actions had undermined public confidence in the electoral institution and called for accountability over the alleged deletion of names from electoral rolls. âIf a match umpire is biased, what is the point of playing?â, Pilot said, questioning how voters could have faith in elections if the neutrality of the institution conducting them was under scrutiny. Watch 'Treason': Kharge BLASTS CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Lists 6 Charges At INDIA Bloc's Mock Parliament He referred to the alleged deletion of 13.3 crore names from electoral rolls, calling it a challenge to the fundamental right to vote. â13.3 crore people's names are known to be struck off the electoral rolls. It's a big challenge to what we believe is the most fundamental issue in our republic, which is the right to vote,â he said. Pilot claimed that the Congress had submitted documentary evidence of alleged wrongdoing by Gyanesh Kumar during his tenure as CEC. âThere has been enough tangible data and documents proof given for the wrongdoings that Gyanesh Kumar has conducted through his term as Chief Election Commissioner,â he said. Pilot questions CEC appointment process, immunity law Pilot also questioned the legal provisions governing the appointment of the CEC and the immunity granted to the office-holder after demitting office. He said the earlier selection process involved the Prime Minister, the leader of opposition and the Chief Justice of India, and questioned the government's decision to change the composition of the selection panel. He also challenged the need for a law granting the CEC immunity after leaving office. âWhat was the need for the government to pass a new law which gives the chief election commissioner immunity for life? Now, he is the only person in the country, not the Prime Minister, not the chief ministers, not the Director of Intelligence or the Army Chief, but the only man who, after demitting office, will have immunity for life,â Pilot said. He alleged that the government had failed to address questions raised by the opposition in Parliament, arguing that the lack of answers had made it necessary to take the issue to the public. âAs a political party, we are within our rights to raise this issue and demand answers,â he said. Congress plans public impeachment proceeding against CEC Pilot said the opposition was seeking to create awareness, particularly among young people, about the importance of independent electoral institutions. He maintained that institutions expected to function transparently should remain above political affiliations. He also said the legal challenge was already under way, with cases pending before the Supreme Court. âThe fight is already going on at multiple levels. We also went to the Supreme Court. The cases are ongoing and are sub judice. The Election Commission has also given a clarification, which obviously you are not convinced about,â he said. title: 'Will deal with Modi, Shah': Rahul Gandhi explains why CEC Gyanesh Kumar is his first target
text: Rahul Gandhi warned the CEC and other officials against assuming that constitutional immunity would shield them from accountability. NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah may be at the top of the political chain of command, but Rahul Gandhi has made it clear that the opposition's first target is Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. Explaining why the INDIA bloc has upped its attack on the election chief, the Congress leader accused him of acting as an instrument of the ruling establishment and warned that those allegedly involved in undermining democratic institutions would be held accountable. We will deal with them, but you are their instruments, and so you are our first target," Rahul Gandhi said on Saturday at the INDIA bloc event in Delhi, where opposition leaders held a symbolic public impeachment of Gyanesh Kumar. The leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha warned the CEC and other officials against assuming that constitutional immunity would shield them from accountability. "So if Mr Gyanesh Kumar thinks, or the five or seven people below him think, that immunity will save them, I would kindly suggest to them, with love and affection, to take a look at what is going on in the country. Please understand the mood of the people outside. You will see tomorrow itself," he said. Rahul Gandhi was referring to the opposition's planned march and public rally in Delhi on Sunday, which he described as an opportunity for a united opposition to demonstrate public anger over alleged electoral irregularities. "A united opposition is going to show you exactly what the mood of the people of this country is," he said. 'We are not going to let you escape' Rahul Gandhi said the opposition's action against CEC was not an isolated protest against one constitutional functionary but part of a larger fight over what he alleged was the misuse of democratic institutions. "You can continue to rig the elections. You can continue to control and allow the misuse of the CBI, the ED, and every single institution of this country. But we guarantee you that this is a temporary phenomenon," he said. The Congress leader insisted that Gyanesh Kumar was only one among several people the opposition held responsible for what it described as an assault on the country's democratic institutions. "We are not going to let you escape. I also want to address the people who have carried out this assault on the Union of India. Gyanesh Kumar is just one element; there are many others. We know who they are, and we understand deeply who they are," Rahul Gandhi said. "This is a warning to you: things are shifting. Please hear this warning and realise that this is a new political weapon sitting in the garden, and this weapon is going to hurt you very badly if you continue down your path," he said. "I am saying this with love and affection; we are not nasty or evil people, but we will protect the Constitution and the voice of our people." Rahul Gandhi also backed the demand for legal action against the CEC, saying Gyanesh Kumar should not only face impeachment but also be tried in court for treason. "I fully support the motion that Mr Gyanesh Kumar should not only be impeached but should also be tried in a court of law for treason so that justice can be served," he said. INDIA bloc holds 'public impeachment' of CEC Rahul Gandhi's remarks came at an unprecedented INDIA bloc event in which opposition MPs and leaders, along with civil society representatives, passed a resolution seeking Gyanesh Kumar's impeachment and accusing him of facilitating the deletion of voters' names to influence election outcomes. The symbolic proceedings were held at the lawns of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence at 10, Rajaji Marg in New Delhi. Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar presided over the meeting, which was organised in a setting resembling parliamentary proceedings. The resolution was moved by Kharge, seconded by Samajwadi Party leader Harendra Malik and supported by Rahul Gandhi and several other opposition MPs and civil society members. It was adopted unanimously by a show of hands. Around 250 opposition MPs, civil society representatives and mediapersons attended the event. Some people who alleged that their names had been wrongly deleted from electoral rolls were also present. Rahul Gandhi acknowledged that holding what resembled parliamentary proceedings outside Parliament might appear unusual, but said the opposition had been left with little choice. "I don't think anything like this has ever happened in history," he said, adding that the gathering of opposition leaders and civil society members in a garden might appear absurd. "But we had no other option, as every single institution is closed to us," he said. The stage was designed to resemble the old Lok Sabha chamber, with a wooden-panelled backdrop and seats arranged in a semi-circular formation. Kharge, who moved the motion, alleged that the right to vote was under threat because the Election Commission was functioning at the behest of PM Modi and Shah. He accused the poll panel of failing to act independently and raised concerns over alleged electoral manipulation. title: INDIA bloc 'impeaches' CEC in mock Parliament, but what will it take to remove him for real
text: NEW DELHI: The opposition on Saturday unanimously passed a "resolution" to remove Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls during a "mock Parliament" organised at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence. Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar presided over the proceedings, with several MPs and activists supporting the demand for the CEC's removal. Watch 'Treason': Kharge BLASTS CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Lists 6 Charges At INDIA Bloc's Mock Parliament Kharge moved the resolution seeking Kumar's removal, accusing him of centralising control over electoral rolls and acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah. Kharge also said that SIR was initiated to remove voters opposed to Bharatiya Janata Party. "The proposal we are bringing today is to safeguard the dignity of a constitutional institution. We have no personal enmity with the CEC. Our intention is that the Election Commission should function impartially in keeping with the spirit of the Constitution," Kharge said. "The trust of the common man in it should remain intact. No one sitting in Delhi should be able to wrongly delete the voting rights of weaker sections, women, and youth using a computer," he added. Meanwhile, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi delivered the closing remarks of the proceedings, describing the event as the opposition's political weapon targeting CEC Gyanesh Kumar, PM Modi and Amit Shah. "This looks like a meeting of Lok Sabha MPs, Rajya Sabha MPs, and common citizens. But actually, this is a political weapon," Rahul said. In the "mock Parliament" at Kharge's residence, the opposition sailed through the resolution with a voice vote. But while the numbers may have been on its side there, would the same motion stand a chance in the real Parliament? What will it take to remove CEC Gyanesh Kumar for real The removal of a CEC is deliberately difficult. Article 324(5) of the Constitution states that the Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office only "in like manner and on the like grounds as a judge of the Supreme Court." "The other Election Commissioners shall not be removed from office except on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner," it further says. The CEC can be removed by the same procedure as a Supreme Court judge and requires a majority vote from both the Houses. Article 124(4) of the Constitution, which lays down the procedure for removing a Supreme Court judge, states that a judge can be removed only by an order of the President following an address by each House of Parliament. Such an address must be supported by a majority of the total membership of that House and by a majority of at least two-thirds of members present and voting, in the same session, on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity. The process begins with a notice of motion in either House of Parliament alleging misbehaviour or incapacity. The notice must be signed by at least 100 MPs in the Lok Sabha or 50 MPs in the Rajya Sabha. The presiding officer of the concerned House can admit or refuse the motion after considering the material and information available. If the motion is admitted, an inquiry is conducted into the charges by a committee constituted for the purpose. Once both Houses pass the motion in accordance with these requirements, an address is made to the President, who then issues the order removing the CEC. The President's role at this stage is constitutional and formal once Parliament has passed the required address. Interestingly, this is not the first time when the opposition is gearing up for introducing a resolution seeking CEC's removal. On April 7, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and Rajya Sabha Chairperson CP Radhakrishnan had rejected opposition notice, which was signed by 130 Lok Sabha members, 63 Rajya Sabha members, seeking the CEC's removal over alleged partisanship and arbitrariness in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. title: Amit Shah visits Delhi police headquarters amid law and order concerns
text: Amit Shah visits Delhi police HQ amid law and order scrutiny NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah visited the Delhi Police headquarters on Jai Singh Road on Saturday to meet senior police officials and discuss the law and order situation in the national capital. title: 'Guilty of centralising electoral rolls': Mallikarjun Kharge lists 6 charges against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, makes 3 demands
text: Kharge accused the CEC of centralising control over electoral rolls and acting at the behest of PM Modi. NEW DELHI: Leader of the opposition in Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge on Saturday accused Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar of facilitating "vote theft" and listed six charges against him at a symbolic "public impeachment" organised by the opposition INDIA bloc. Kharge alleged that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls was initiated to remove voters opposed to the BJP. The proceedings began at his residence on Rajaji Marg, with former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar chairing the event. Kharge accused the CEC of centralising control over electoral rolls and acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah. Watch 'Treason': Kharge BLASTS CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Lists 6 Charges At INDIA Bloc's Mock Parliament During the proceedings, Kharge listed six allegations against Kumar: Conspired to steal elections Deleted 13.3 crore voters Rewrote Form 6 without parliamentary oversight or knowledge Seized the electoral rolls through ECINET Breached his constitutional mandate and shut out the two other election commissioners Acted at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Amit Shah Kharge also reiterated the opposition's three demands: The removal of the CEC An end to the SIR exercise Changes to the 2023 law governing the appointment of the chief election commissioner. Kharge also accused PM Modi government of using various means to retain power since 2014, including defections, splitting parties, misuse of central agencies and alleged electoral irregularities. "The proposal we are bringing today is to safeguard the dignity of a constitutional institution. We have no personal enmity with the CEC. Our intention is that the Election Commission should function impartially in keeping with the spirit of the Constitution. The trust of the common man in it should remain intact. No one sitting in Delhi should be able to wrongly delete the voting rights of weaker sections, women, and youth using a computer," Kharge posted on X. He further alleged that the government had repeatedly tried to retain power through various means. "The Modi government has hatched every conspiracy since 2014 to cling to power: stealing MPs, breaking parties, stealing governments, Electoral Bonds, misuse of ED/CBI. And now Vote Theftâcut opposition votes and rule. There are hundreds of examples of Vote Theft," he said. Kharge also criticised the 2023 law governing the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC), alleging that it provided the election commissioner with legal protection. "Gyanesh Kumar is able to carry out this theft because of the 2023 CEC Act. In December 2023, this bill was passed by suspending 145 opposition MPs. This law gives the CEC a lifelong protective shield that even the President and CJI do not have," he added. Questioning the results of the 2024 Maharashtra and Haryana assembly elections, Kharge alleged that the INDIA bloc's strong performance in the Lok Sabha elections was followed by a reversal in the state polls due to electoral irregularities. "In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, we had an excellent performance in Maharashtra and Haryana, but the results flipped in the assembly elections. Reasonâvotes were illegally added before the elections and then all names were removed. This work is being done together by Modi-Shah and Gyanesh," he alleged. title: 'Gyanesh, when will you vanish?': Mamata mocks CEC; Akhilesh invokes Haldighati - who said what at INDIA bloc rally
text: 'Bengal is victim of SIR,' says Mamata Banerjee at INDIA bloc rally. NEW DELHI: Leaders of the INDIA bloc on Sunday held a mega rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, targeting Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and opposing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The rally held over allegations of âvote choriâ, saw senior INDIA bloc leaders accuse the BJP of electoral manipulation and undermining democratic institutions. Watch âModi Hatao, Democracy Bachaoâ: Kharge Leads INDIA Bloc Attack On BJP Over âVote Choriâ Claims Today Several opposition leaders targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and CEC Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that the Election Commission was favouring the ruling party. They demanded Kumar's removal and vowed to continue their campaign against him. 'Gyanesh, when will you vanish?' Mamata mocks CEC Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee accused the BJP of trying to influence the West Bengal elections and vowed to fight against the alleged actions. âBengal is victim of SIR. We will not spare them, we will fight,â she said, adding, âGyanesh, when will you vanish?â Mamata also accused the BJP of looting funds linked to the Ram Janmabhoomi and Waqf properties, and alleged that the police had become the party's âcomradesâ. âWhat haven't they looted? They looted the money of Ram Janmabhoomi, Waqf properties... The police became their comrades. The BJP has no organisation of its own. That is why they make the police do party work. Agencies don't work with the BJP. The BJP will go,â she said. Accusing the BJP of undermining democracy and the Constitution through alleged âvote theftâ, Mamata said the party had also deprived young people of jobs, compromised women's dignity and misused donations. âThese people have looted the country's democracy and constitution through 'vote theft', and attacked it on top of that. The BJP has stolen youth's jobs, stolen women's honor, stolen donationsâwe must remove them from power,â she said. âBengal is the victim of the circumstances of this SIR. We will not give up. We will give our lives, we will fight, but we will not surrender. They looted our Bengal. We will save democracy and bring it back... We will take revenge through politics. We will take revenge through democracy. We will fight...â she added. 'After Gyanesh, you're next': Rahul warns PM Modi, Shah Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi also targeted PM Modi, Amit Shah and Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that the Election Commission had helped the BJP manipulate elections. âListen to me. What I say always turns out to be true, doesn't it? I am telling every citizen and every youth of India: Gyanesh Kumar will be removed from the post of Chief Election Commissioner. Gyanesh Kumar will go to jail,â he said. He also alleged that PM Modi and Amit Shah would not have reached their current positions without Kumar's help. âWithout Gyanesh Kumar, neither Narendra Modi would have become Prime Minister nor Amit Shah would have become Home Minister,â Rahul said. Rahul said the opposition was not driven by hatred towards the BJP leadership but was fighting to protect the Constitution and the rights of citizens. âWe do not hate Narendra Modi, Amit Shah or Gyanesh Kumar. We are people who open the shop of love, not hatred. We are people of non-violence. For me, there is no enemy. Neither Narendra Modi, nor Amit Shah, nor Gyanesh Kumar. But the voice of every citizen of India is more important to me, even more important than religion. That is my religion,â he said. He added that the INDIA bloc would not resort to violence or spread hatred but would continue to oppose any attempt to undermine the Constitution. âWe will not use violence, we will not harm anyone and we will not spread hatred. We will work with love. But we will not let you destroy the Constitution. No matter what happens, we will not let it happen,â Rahul said. Rahul also raised concerns over unemployment, farmers' rights and the concentration of wealth, alleging that the country's resources were increasingly in the hands of a few people. âThe farmer is not getting his rights. The youth are not getting employment. The labourer is not getting his rights, and the entire wealth has gone into the hands of two or three people. We do not want such an India, and we will not accept such an India,â he said. He said the country should ensure that farmers received the benefits of their hard work and that students who worked hard had access to employment. âAnyone can join Shiv ki Baraat. Every living being can join it. Can anyone be stopped from participating in that? No. We want that kind of India. If a farmer works hard, he should reap the rewards. If a student studies for 18 hours, they should get employment. We do not want a country that belongs only to two or three people,â Rahul said. Referring to Amit Shah's remarks that PM Modi would remain in power, Rahul said the opposition would continue its campaign after demanding action against the CEC. âAmit Shah ji said Narendra Modi is not going anywhere. I am telling you the opposite: Narendra Modi cannot go anywhere. Even if he wants to leave, we will not let him go. After Gyanesh Kumar, we are going to stand right in front of you. Legal action will be taken against them,â he said. Rahul described Kumar's removal as the first step towards putting the country back on the right track. âThe first step to get the country back on the right track is to remove Gyanesh Kumar,â he said. Kharge accuses Modi, Shah of shielding CEC Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge alleged that the BJP government had come to power through a âstolenâ mandate. He said removing Prime Minister Narendra Modi was necessary to protect democracy. Kharge accused Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah of attempting to take away the voting rights of Dalits, women and young people. He alleged that the two leaders were shielding CEC Gyanesh Kumar. âModi and Shah have attempted to snatch the vote of Dalits, youth and women. Modi ji wants to take away their votes through his man -- Ganesh Kumar. We will keep fighting until he goes, and ensure his exit,â Kharge said. He further alleged that the BJP-led governments at the Centre and in Maharashtra, Bihar and Uttar Pradesh had been formed through âvote choriâ. âBe it the central government, governments in Maharashtra, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, they are 'chori' governments (formed on stolen mandate). We have to throw out these 'vote chor',â he said. Kharge also said the opposition would continue its agitation until Kumar resigned. title: INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan saw creative expression take centre stage as slogans, posters and placards delivered the message
text: Ramlila Maidan became the space for INDIA bloc members to make their presence felt NEW DELHI: If the stage at Ramlila Maidan sent out a strong message of a united opposition that will not relent till it sees Gyanesh Kumar's removed as Chief Election Commissioner, the atmosphere at the packed grounds reflected the same sense of coming together as flags of all hues representing the diverse ideologies of INDIA parties were held up by workers and supporters. From slogans like "Vote Chor Gaddi Chhod" to the euphoric response of the crowd to repeated chanting of "Inquilab Zindabad" - the Ramlila Maidan on Sunday became the space for INDIA bloc members to make their presence felt. The RJD and Samajwadi Party flags shared space with a sea of flags representing the Left parties - a reflection of how diverse ideologies and ideas converged on ground for a common cause. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi got the loudest applause from the crowd that had been growing strong since 9 in the morning and remained eager to stay even as the main speeches only took off at 3 pm as the top leaders of the INDIA parties arrived on stage after the Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao March from CP Minto Road Junction to the rally venue. With 2027 set to see crucial assembly polls in UP, Punjab and Uttarakhand, one saw Samajwadi Party supporters assert their presence as they rooted for party supremo Akhilesh Yadav cheering loudly and waving the Party flag. Yadav delivered a fiery speech shooting sharply at Modi saying, "Jo UP sey aayey they woh UP sey hi jayengey". He also raised the issue of "chanda chori" from Ram Temple Trust in Ayodhya. Reflecting on the INDIA campaign so far, CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya was the first speaker who set the set the tone by highlighting how the parties in the Alliance have unitedly taken up and build the outreach on the issue of SIR and working of Election Commission under CEC Gyanesh Kumar. "We took the decision to hit the streets on Sept 30 at the INDIA bloc meeting and since then the slogan of "vote chor gaddi chhod" and "vote bachao, desh bachao" has resonated across the country. Since they started SIR in Bihar people have suffered and faced its impact and to counter it and the autocratic working of the Central govt, the people have responded with this "jan sailaab" he highlighted. Bhattacharya and CPI(M) general secretary MA Baby referred to the ongoing protests as nothing short of a second freedom struggle. RJD's Tejashwi Yadav chose to draw from the epic Mahabharat to make his point. "Vote chori key liyey Mahabharat ka ayojan kiya Hai Ramlila Maidan mein..," he said in Hindi. He cited the example of Shakuni and his dice to highlight that there was a lack of a level-playing field there and alleged that the same situation existed in the Modi regime with Gyanesh Kumar as CEC. He demanded that Gyanesh Kumar should be tried for treason. Rahul Gandhi had raised this at the public impeachment on Saturday and reiterated the same on Sunday. Interestingly, TMC chairperson and former West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee while delivering a fiery attack on CEC Gyanesh Kumar, was the only speaker who after highlighting the unity in the INDIA bloc, lauded and backed the efforts of the Cockroach Janta Party and Gen Z in taking up issues ranging from concerns in the examination system to SIR and EC related protests. It was interesting to see a large presence of youth with student outfits. The Left linked student wings like AISA, SFI, AISF and Krantkari Yuva Sangathan joined with full fervour alongside the NSUI. One one side there were the Left students groups who chose to break into an impromtu performance amid the crowd as all waited for the INDIA leaders to arrive. Then one saw a large group of ethnically dressed women and men from Jharkhand play their traditional instruments. title: From Mallikarjun Kharge's lawn, 250 opposition MPs 'impeach' CEC Gyanesh Kumar
text: INDIA bloc functionaries take part in the proceedings during the âpublic impeachmentâ programme against CEC Gyanesh Kumar at the residence of Mallikarjun Kharge in New Delhi Saturday NEW DELHI: With Rahul Gandhi terming "public impeachment" and Sunday's Ramlila Maidan rally a "dangerous political weapon" targeting Modi-Shah-Gyanesh, the INDIA bloc, in a symbolic move, Saturday passed a "resolution" to "impeach" CEC Gyanesh Kumar accusing it of colluding with the ruling BJP to compromise national election management. It also sought that Kumar be "tried for treason". Six "charges" of "premeditated attack on poll process" - as part of "criminal conspiracy" of BJP, PM Modi and Union minister Amit Shah - span questionable handling of poll rolls, "manipulated" SIR to delete 14 crore voters, illegal changes to Form 6 to block new voters, deletion of voters through software. CEC Kumar has also been accused of ignoring the two ECs in decision making. The venue was designed with Parliament chamber like decor, with former Speaker Meira Kumar in the high chair. LoP Rajya Sabha Kharge tabled the resolution while Rahul concluded the debate, before Meira Kumar put the resolution to vote that was passed by a voice vote. The slogan 'vote chor gaddi chhod' ended the assembly after three hours of debate. Setting the tone, Kharge said Modi has hatched conspiracies to retain power, which include engineering defections, splitting parties, electoral bonds, misuse of agencies, while adding the 2023 "immunity law" for the CEC is another such instrument. Underlining the need for "public impeachment", Kharge said RS and LS rejected the opposition notices for removal of Kumar. title: Punjab assembly passes resolution against CEC over âvoter deletionsâ, demands inquiry
text: Punjab assembly passes resolution against CEC over âvoter deletionsâ, demands inquiry Chandigarh: The Punjab assembly on Friday passed a resolution expressing concern over incidents of citizens allegedly being deprived of their right to vote, demanding an âindependent, impartial, and credibleâ investigative mechanism to probe alleged irregularities in electoral rolls and voter deletions under Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. The resolution, moved by finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema, expressed concern over the functioning of the Election Commission and accused the CEC of âtearing apart the Constitutionâ and acting to deprive Indian citizens of their fundamental democratic right to vote. In the absence of BJP MLAs, the Punjab govt claimed that the resolution was passed âunanimouslyâ by voice vote. Congress MLAs had staged a walkout earlier during the sitting. Two rebel Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) MLAsâManpreet Singh Ayali and Sukhwinder Kumar Sukhiâalong with BSP MLA Nacchatar Pal, supported the resolution. Speaking on the resolution, chief minister Bhagwant Mann termed it a âserious concern for democracyâ that the govt is now deciding who gets to vote, reversing the democratic norm where citizens elect their govt. He further alleged that over 14 crore votes were arbitrarily deleted during the special intensive revision (SIR) process without providing any justification. Cheema alleged that during the last Delhi elections, over 40,000 votes in AAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal âs constituency were deleted, which resulted in him losing the election. âThe BJP indulged in âvote choriâ through the EC to come to power in Delhi. The same strategy was subsequently used in Bihar and West Bengal,â he alleged. Invoking Articles 324, 325 and 326 of the Constitutionâwhich guarantee adult suffrage, non-discrimination in voter list preparation, and the supervision of the electoral processâthe resolution emphasised that democracy is built on equality, justice and the sovereignty of the people. Expressing concern over nationwide complaints regarding the large-scale deletion of eligible citizensâ names from electoral rolls, the House questioned the âtransparency, impartiality, and accountabilityâ of the EC. Through the resolution, the House expressed concern over citizens allegedly being deprived of their right to vote and demanded that constitutional protection of the voting rights of eligible citizens be ensured. Second, it called for the setting up of an independent, impartial and credible investigative mechanism to inquire into alleged irregularities in the electoral process and voter roll revisions under CEC Gyanesh Kumar, aiming to fix accountability. The House also demanded that if concrete evidence of criminal violations emerges during the investigation against any individual, criminal proceedings should be initiated under applicable laws. The assembly appealed to the Centre and constitutional authorities to preserve the independence and impartiality of the EC. Copies of the resolution are being dispatched to President, Prime Minister and the CEC for necessary action. âB R Ambedkar gave every citizen an equal right to vote through the Constitution, but Gyanesh Kumar, while tearing apart the Constitution, has worked to deprive this right from the citizens of India,â read the resolution. title: SIR row: Supreme Court defers hearing, grants petitioner 10 days to reply to EC's counter-affidavit
text: SC granted petitioner 10 days to respond to the ECâs defence of its functioning and the SIR exercise, deferring the hearing until after Diwali NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has deferred hearing on a batch of petitions challenging the functioning of the Election Commission (EC), including allegations that Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar took unilateral decisions on matters that required unanimous approval, particularly in connection with the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. A bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant granted petitioner Rakesh Kumar Singh 10 days to file a rejoinder to the ECâs counter-affidavit, which was submitted on Monday night. Senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for the petitioner, sought time to respond to the poll body's submissions. Watch EC Makes 4 Changes To SSR Amid Anti-CEC Protests; Congress Says âToo Little, Too Lateâ The matter is likely to be listed on November 17, after the Diwali vacation and completion of the 10-day period. The petitions challenge the ECâs decision-making process and seek to invalidate the SIR exercise and related actions. Singhâs plea also sought the suspension of the CEC over allegations of unilateral decision-making. What the EC told SC In its counter-affidavit, the EC defended its functioning and the conduct of the SIR exercise, rejecting allegations of irregularities and questioning the basis of the petition. The affidavit was unanimously approved by Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. The EC said all three SIR orders issued in June 2025, October 2025 and May 2026 were unanimous decisions of the Commission. The poll body also maintained that notes, queries or suggestions made by individual commissioners while files are being processed do not constitute decisions of the Commission. It said files are routed through one Election Commissioner, then the other, and finally the CEC, while urgent approvals may be obtained electronically and recorded on file later. On allegations concerning changes to voter enrolment forms, the EC said Form 6 had not been amended and that only the Centre could make such changes. However, it acknowledged that the online display could be interpreted as an amendment and said that, from October 21, the online application would be split into Form 6 and a separate SIR declaration, in line with the physical form. The Commission also said voters whose records could not be mapped during the SIR need not attend hearings as a rule, with booth-level officers (BLOs) collecting documents from their homes. text: Protesters from Karnataka participated in a national rally against alleged voter deletions from electoral rolls BENGALURU: Bringing Karnataka's voter-deletion row to the national stage, protesters from the state joined the INDIA bloc's march in Delhi on Sunday, carrying what they described as the âlongest listâ of names deleted from electoral rolls. The delegation's participation comes amid growing opposition to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter lists, with the INDIA bloc accusing the Election Commission of allowing eligible voters to be removed. Watch Amit Shah Slams Congress Rally On 1984 Riots Anniversary, Says It Rubs Salt Into Victimsâ Wounds The protest, held at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, is part of the Opposition's nationwide campaign against alleged electoral irregularities. INDIA bloc leaders are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, alleging large-scale voter deletions and questioning the Election Commission's independence. The march began from the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction, with senior Opposition leaders, including Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, Abhishek Banerjee and KC Venugopal, heading towards Ramlila Maidan. The rally is being attended by leaders and supporters of several INDIA bloc parties. Over 99 lakh fewer voters in final electoral roll The Karnataka delegation's protest comes days after the state published its final electoral roll following the SIR exercise. The final list, released on October 27, recorded 4.54 crore electors, compared with 5.54 crore before the revision â a reduction of nearly 99.76 lakh voters. According to the Chief Electoral Officer's data, 1.08 crore enumeration forms were not included in the final roll. Separately, 61,867 electors were declared ineligible after notices were issued and hearings conducted. The exercise also saw 10.08 lakh voters added and 1.88 lakh names deleted during the claims and objections period. The Election Commission has maintained that the revision was intended to verify voter eligibility and update electoral rolls. The Opposition, however, has alleged that eligible voters risk being excluded through the exercise and has demanded that the SIR process be scrapped and eligible voters whose names were deleted be restored to the electoral rolls. INDIA bloc demands CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation The November 1 rally follows a symbolic public impeachment programme held by Opposition MPs on October 31 at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence. Around 250 INDIA bloc MPs participated in the proceedings, which were modelled on parliamentary debates and culminated in a resolution accusing the CEC of facilitating electoral manipulation. The exercise was symbolic and did not constitute a formal impeachment proceeding. The INDIA bloc had called on supporters, including students, youth, women and workers, to join the 'Chalo Dilli' march. Opposition parties projected a turnout of up to 10 lakh, while Delhi Police estimated around 50,000 participants. More than 4,000 police personnel were deployed around Ramlila Maidan and the march route. title: 'We know everything': SC on pleas alleging unilateral decisions by CEC, gives petitioners 10 days to reply
text: The three-judge bench adjourned the hearing to November 17. NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday said that it would examine all aspects of the Election Commission of India 's (ECI) decision-making process amid allegations that key decisions, including those related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls were taken without the unanimous consent. "We know everything. We will examine," Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said while hearing a batch of petitions challenging the functioning of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the poll panel, Live Law reported. Watch EC Makes 4 Changes To SSR Amid Anti-CEC Protests; Congress Says âToo Little, Too Lateâ The three-judge bench, comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, adjourned the hearing to November 17. The top court granted the petitioners 10 days to file rejoinders to the ECIâs counter-affidavit, which was submitted on Monday and asserted that the decisions in question were unanimous. The CJI's remark came after senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi, appearing for leader of opposition on Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders, urged the court to direct the ECI to preserve file notings and internal communications related to its decisions. Singhvi argued that the records were crucial to determining whether the decisions concerning the SIR were taken unanimously or unilaterally. "This whole issue depends on the decision-making process, consultation, and whether the decision was unanimous or not unanimous. Let file notings, etc be preserved," Singhvi added. The petitions challenge the functioning of Gyanesh Kumar alleged that several ECI decisions, including those related to the SIR, were issued without the concurrence of the other two Election Commissioners. The bench also issued notices to the ECI and other respondents on a fresh petition filed by Rajya Sabha MP Dola Sen. The plea alleges that changes were made to Form 6 during the Bihar SIR without the Supreme Courtâs approval. Senior advocate and MP Maneka Guruswamy, appearing for Sen, told the court that the poll panel had wrongly claimed that the changes to Form 6 were approved by the top court. The CJI said the court would examine all the issues and asked senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for the first petitioner, Rakesh Kumar Singh to file a rejoinder within 10 days to the ECIâs reply affidavit. Earlier on Monday, in its 248-page affidavit, the ECI strongly defended the SIR and rejected allegations that Form 6, the statutory form used for voter registration, had been amended. "The attempt to make aspersions against the Election Commission is unfortunate," the affidavit, filed by Deputy Election Commissioner Bhanu Prakash Yeturu on behalf of the ECI said, PTI reported. The poll panel also maintained that no changes had been made to the statutory Form 6. It said the affidavit itself had been approved for filing through a unanimous decision of all three Election Commissioners. title: 'Keep Rahul Gandhi mock PM for life': BJP's dig at INDIA bloc's 'public impeachment' of CEC
text: "Keep him as your mock Prime Minister for life," Sambit Patra's dig at Rahul Gandhi. NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) on Saturday took a dig at the Congress , saying that the party should keep Rahul Gandhi a "mock prime minister for life". Holding a press briefing parallel to the proceedings of the INDIA bloc's "public impeachment" of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, BJP national spokesperson Sambit Patra said: "The world has already realised that Rahul Gandhi lacks the fuel. This satellite will never launch. Keep him as your mock Prime Minister for life. We have no objection." Patra said the programme by the Congress-led bloc was "a mockery of the Parliament itself". Watch Rahul Gandhi Targets BJP Over Connaught Place Shutdown During INDIA Blocâs âChalo Dilliâ March Today Tearing into the Congress party, Patra defended the law that lends immunity and protection to CEC Gyanesh Kumar, saying the BJP "did not introduce any law that did not already exist. Immunity and protection for the President and the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) are already enshrined in the Constitution". Patra also cited the August 2023 Telangana lower special court order that directed an FIR to be filed against the Chief Election Commissioner. "The high court immediately quashed the order, stating that this was not the correct procedure and directed that it be dismissed. But it became evident then that, due to political pressure, anyone could file a case or an FIR against individuals, even those holding high constitutional offices who are protected by the Constitution, without any regard for the law. Therefore, a procedure was introduced. It was merely a procedure. The legal provision already existed within the Constitution. The Constitution of India provides this protection," he said. BJP MP Ravi Shankar Prasad slammed Rahul Gandhi for making "a mockery of the people of the country" and dared him to resign. "These individuals do not participate in parliamentary discussions; instead, they are making a mockery of the people of the country... Nehru ji became Prime Minister by stealing votes... How long will you continue to ridicule constitutional institutions? When a decision goes in your favor, the Election Commission seems 'fine' to you... This is shameful. I challenge Rahul Gandhiâif you have the courage, you should resign," the BJP leader told news agency ANI. 'Mock parliament a drama' Addressing a press brief, BJP national spokesperson Sambit Patra said: "If there was ever a vote theft in India, it was committed by the first member of the Gandhi family, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, who stole the votes of prominent Congress leaders. Those leaders had cast their votes in a ballot box to elect Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel as Prime Minister. By stealing those votes, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru became the Prime Minister of the country, an unelected Prime Minister. " Patra, who is MP from Puri Lok Sabha constituency, called the "mock parliament" a "drama", and highlighted that the Speical Intensive Revision (SIR) was ongoing and substantiated the claims around the "13 crore delted voters". "Across various states, the names of 13 crore people have not yet been included in the final electoral roll. Why is this the case? What is this 'ASDD' formula? 'A' stands for 'Absent'. There is an official known as a BLO (Booth Level Officer). The BLO is responsible for an 'enumeration form' that every individual is required to complete. The BLO visits your home three times with this form. If you are not present on any of these three occasions, you are marked as 'absent', and your name is excluded from the electoral roll. What about 'S' in 'ASDD'? It stands for 'Shifted'âpermanently shifted," Patra said. Amit Shah challenges Rahul, Akhilesh Earlier, Union home minister Amit Shah slammed Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav for raising the issue of voter irregularities ahead of the INDIA bloc's Delhi Chalo march and challenged them to discuss the issue during a special session of Parliament. While addressing a gathering in Uttar Pradesh's Lucknow, Shah highlighted the BJP's electoral victories in states like Haryana, Maharashtra and Bihar, and said that the opposition had realised that it could not win elections. "In Haryana, the Bharatiya Janata Party formed the government after securing the highest number of seats. In Maharashtra, the NDA formed the government with the largest share of seats. In Bihar, for the first time, a chief minister from the Bharatiya Janata Party took office. In Delhi, the Bharatiya Janata Party formed the government after three decades. In Puducherry, the Bharatiya Janata Party formed the government once again. In Assam, we achieved a hat-trick by winning 100 seats, and in Bengal, we completely wiped out Mamata Didi," Shah said. "After the events in Bengal, they have realised that they simply cannot win elections," he added. The Union home minister said that "Rahul Baba" and Akhilesh were cut from different cloth and accused them of "blaming the umpire" instead of accepting defeat. "Naturally, when a team loses a match or a game, they should sit down and practise more - that is what is expected, isn't it? But 'Rahul Baba' is cut from a different cloth. The same goes for Akhilesh and others in the 'INDIA' alliance who are with him. Instead of accepting defeat, they began accusing the umpire of cheating, claiming that votes were stolen," Shah said. He further said that the opposition had no intention of raising the issue in Parliament and accused it of refusing to let the House function. "Rahul Baba, I challenge both you and Akhilesh Yadav right here and now: the Bharatiya Janata Party is fully prepared to discuss this in Parliament. We have nothing to hide. Let us convene a special session of Parliament - but they have no intention of speaking there. They refuse to let Parliament function; instead, they just create a ruckus," Shah said. title: June 2025 decision to hold SIR taken unanimously, EC tells SC
text: EC tells SC that the June 24, 2025 decision to conduct nationwide SIR was unanimous, denying opposition claims that CEC Gyanesh Kumar acted unilaterally. NEW DELHI: The Election Commission Monday filed an affidavit in SC that the chief election commissioner and the two election commissioners had unanimously taken the decision on June 24, 2025 to conduct nationwide SIR of electoral rolls and that there was no difference of opinion. The affidavit by deputy EC Bhanu Prakash Yeturu came with an unusual declaration that it was being filed with the approval of the CEC and the two ECs. âAt the very outset, I state that the present affidavit has been approved for filing before the SC by a unanimous decision of the three members of the Election Commission, that is the 2 election commissioners and the chief election commissioner,â the affidavit said. Watch EC Makes 4 Changes To SSR Amid Anti-CEC Protests; Congress Says âToo Little, Too Lateâ The assertion contradicts the charge that CEC Gyanesh Kumar, at Modi governmentâs instance, unilaterally decided to conduct SIR of electoral rolls â the mainstay of the oppositionâs âvote choriâ campaign. The affidavit was filed in response to petitions, including one filed by Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders, following a news report that the two ECs â S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi â had approached the cabinet secretary because of their differences with the CEC over SIR-related issues. âAllegations based on the communication between ECs and the cabinet secretary are misconceived,â the EC said, adding that the letters by Sandhu and Joshi pertained to administrative matters. No substance in claim that Form 6 was amended by SIR orders: EC An office order came to be issued on July 28 by an IAS officer of the rank of additional secretary who had been posted on deputation to the commission pertaining to internal work allocation. On July 29, the two election commissioners wrote separate letters to the cabinet secretary in relation to this order and the conduct of the officer. In view of the joint direction of July 30 by the two ECs, the order of July 28 was never implemented,â the commission said. Responding to the petitions by Rahul and other INDIA bloc netas, the EC said all the petitions were based on a news article alleging that the commission had not been functioning in accordance with the procedure mandated in law, and allegations were also made questioning the integrity of the commission. It also issued a strong denial of the allegation, another key plank of the oppositionâs offensive, that Form 6, as provided under Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, was amended by the commission by the SIR orders of June 24 and Oct 27 last year and May 14 this year. âThere is no substance in the contention that Form 6 has been amended by the commission vide the SIR orders.â EC said Form 6 could be amended only by the Centre and what was changed was the introduction of a declaration to âenable the person seeking registration as a voter to dispense with the need for filing documents during the claims and objections periodâ. The âdeclarationâ was a document provided by the SIR orders and was not a part of Form 6, which was the statutory form for inclusion in the electoral rolls, it said, adding there was no significant change in the earlier and present declaration. The declaration that the affidavit was approved by the two ECs is significant because of the charge that the CECâs âunilateralâ calls on SIR-related issues were violative of the law, which required the poll body to take decisions unanimously or, when not possible, by majority. The opposition has demanded removal and prosecution of Gyanesh Kumar for violating the law. Denying the charge, the affidavit said that while the CEC, the ECs and even other officers may have expressed different views during deliberations, the decisions were taken in accordance with law. âThe views by ECs/CEC of the commission during the decision-making process on the subjects before them are considered for arriving at the decision. It is upon consideration of all the views placed before the commission that the decision is taken and the orders are issued in accordance with the process,â the EC said. Explaining the process of decision-making in which views of all divisions concerned with the subject are considered in detail, the EC said, âIn any such decision-making process, any suggestion, observation or query by the CEC or ECs either to the ECs or CEC or to any officer of the commission does not constitute a decision of the commission under Section 18 of the CEC and ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023. â It said the statute prefers a decision by unanimity but also provides for decision-making by majority in the three-member EC. The commission said the CEC and ECs had taken a unanimous decision on June 29 that âin case any person to whom notice has been issued during the ongoing SIR, for being unmapped and/or logical discrepancies, BLOs will visit the homes of such persons for collection of documents and thereafter upload them in the ECINet, for decision by the EROâ. title: 'Ball is in their court': Congress asks PM Modi to sack CEC if concerned about Delhi traders
text: NEW DELHI: Congress on Monday said Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union minister Amit Shah must sack Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar if they are genuinely concerned about Delhi's traders and want to stop the INDIA bloc's November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan. The ball is in their court," Khera said. "Protests, rallies and demonstrations demanding an end to ECI-administered Vote Chori and election rigging for the RSS-BJP are acts of patriotism. The protests are not the problem. The problem is the governmentâs obstinacy to save the chair of a bureaucrat who wins elections for them. title: Gyanesh has to go, PM & Shah next, says Rahul Gandhi at anti-CEC rally
text: Around 50,000 people turned up for INDIA blocâs rally in Delhi on Sunday, according to Delhi Police estimates NEW DELHI: In a Ramlila Maidan packed with protesters and ringing with anti-BJP and anti-CEC slogans Sunday, Congress MP Rahul Gandhi said the opposition will confront the top BJP duo of Narendra Modi and Amit Shah after Gyanesh Kumar's removal as chief election commissioner. The trio was losing sleep over the agitation, he claimed, and said the CEC's exit would be the first step in putting the country back on track. With opposition biggies Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge, Sonia Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav, Mamata Banerjee, Tejashwi Yadav, Dipankar Bhattacharya, MA Baby, Farooq Abdullah and Mehbooba Mufti on the dais, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha said the "voice of the people of India" is greater to him than religion, and he will brook no assault on it. Mocking BJP's catchphrase - "Modi kahin nahin jayega" - which was coined in response to Kharge's comment, Rahul said the PM won't be allowed to go anywhere. "You cannot flee... You will stay here and face action." 2024 polls illegal, says Rahul; Modi picking voters: Kharge With a âvote bachao, desh bachaoâ banner forming the backdrop of the dais, the speakers focused on âvote choriâ, repeating allegations about SIR and deletion of around 14 crore voters. Rahul accused the CEC, PM and Shah of suppressing the voice of people through âvote choriâ. While Mamata and Akhilesh said the West Bengal mandate to BJP was âstolenâ, Rahul mentioned the Maharashtra, Haryana, Chhattisgarh, MP and 2024 Lok Sabha polls. He said the 2024 polls were illegal, arguing the difference between NDA and opposition was merely 3%, while 15% of the 2024 voters have been deleted under SIR. âModi is selecting the voters,â Congress chief Kharge said. Led by Kharge, most INDIA bloc members stressed ejecting BJP from office was a must to save democracy, even leading the crowd in âBJP hatao, desh bachaoâ chants. Some reminded the crowd that Ramlila Maidan has been the harbinger of history and change in the past. text: NEW DELHI: Congress on Monday urged the Supreme Court to summon all relevant records related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, following the Election Commission's affidavit stating that all decisions were taken unanimously. title: CEC impeachment: Speaker Om Birla says fresh motion against Gyanesh Kumar will be examined as per rules
text: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla on Thursday said if the opposition brings any fresh impeachment motion against the country's top poll officer, it will be examined according to rules and procedures. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla on Thursday said any fresh motion seeking the impeachment of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar would be examined in accordance with parliamentary rules and procedures, as opposition protests demanding the poll panel chiefâs removal intensified over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The opposition has made two attempts to remove Kumar, with notices in the first attempt rejected by both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha. Notices submitted in the second attempt are still pending in the Upper House. Watch EC Makes 4 Changes To SSR Amid Anti-CEC Protests; Congress Says âToo Little, Too Lateâ âIf any fresh notice comes, we will see and examine it accordingly under rules and procedures,â Birla told a press conference, responding to a question on the possibility of another impeachment motion against the CEC. Protests against Kumar have intensified over the past fortnight, with opposition parties demanding his resignation over alleged irregularities in the revision of electoral rolls. The agitation gathered momentum after The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded objections at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders related to the SIR, alleging that these were issued without their knowledge or recommendation. Under the Constitution, the CEC can be removed only through a parliamentary process similar to that prescribed for the removal of a Supreme Court judge. The Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, also provides for the CEC or an Election Commissioner to resign by submitting a written resignation to the President. The removal process is governed by constitutional provisions and the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968. Once a removal motion is admitted in either House of Parliament, the Speaker or the Rajya Sabha Chairman constitutes a three-member committee to investigate the charges. The panel comprises the Chief Justice of India or a Supreme Court judge, a chief justice of a high court and a distinguished jurist. title: 'Can't occupy a site for all times': SC on Delhi protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
text: A traders' counsel told the court that around 50 lakh people lived in areas surrounding the protest site and claimed that shops remained shut NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday said no protest group can occupy a designated demonstration site indefinitely, observing that the right to protest must be balanced with the rights of other citizens. Hearing pleas filed by traders' associations over the impact of demonstrations in Delhi, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said designated protest venues must be made available to different groups for specific periods. "You can't occupy a site for all times. Where farmers, journalists, etc. will go? Everyone has right to protest. Designated time must be given for designated period," CJI Surya Kant said, according to LiveLaw. The bench also said that orders granting permission for protests must clearly specify the reasons for allowing or refusing them. "You can't prevent other people, that I am doing protest now you can't," the CJI observed. The court was hearing pleas raising concerns over alleged police brutality, mass detentions, the closure of Metro stations and internet shutdowns during protests, besides the impact of demonstrations on businesses. title: Protesters demand SIR rollback, CECâs resignation
text: Economist Parakala Prabhaka during a protest against SIR at Lower Tank Bund in Hyderabad on Saturday Hyderabad: Sitting on the edge of Lower Tank Bund stretch, holding the national flag, 63-year-old Suvamoy Sen had brought along more than just a symbol. âI brought the flag my father used in the Independence movement, when he fought against the British,â he said. Sen was among the 250-300 citizens, civil society members and students who gathered near the Makhdoom Mohiuddin statue on Saturday evening to form a human chain, protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demand the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Organised by the newly formed People Against SIR alliance, the protest was titled âDemanding rollback of SIR and resignation of CEC.â Groups including AIPM, RSV and NAPM, along with student organisations such as SFI and AISA, took part. The lanes along Lower Tank Bund were packed with people, many of them elders attending a protest for the first time. A Hyderabad resident since 2002, Sen said his familyâs own experience had prompted him to join the protest. âMy daughter-in-lawâs name was dropped from the rolls in Hyderabad, and she received a notice. When we approached the BLO, we were told that the system would allow officials to log in only from Delhi, not Hyderabad, and that she should submit Form 6,â he said. Others described similar ordeals. Jyothi Sundeep Mirmire (53), a resident of Himayathnagar who has voted regularly, found her name missing from the draft roll. âI have recently been told that my name has been included in the list, but I am awaiting final roll. I spend nearly half a day at the BLO office getting my details from my hometown, Mysore, verified,â she said. Social worker Zeenat Begum from Old City said the exercise was disrupting peopleâs livelihoods. âI have lost many working days due to running around BLOâs office because of the SIR process,â said Zeenatâs friend Nasreen Kausar, a tailor from Yakutpura. Throughout the protest, participants raised several slogans, including âGyanesh Kumar resign,â as they held hands to form a human chain along the lane. People Against SIR alliance is an all-India platform and civil society coalition recently formed to oppose the SIR. It comprises farmersâ organisations, trade and workersâ unions, student groups, womenâs organisations and groups representing Dalits, Adivasis, minorities, persons with disabilities and transgender people. Meanwhile, Iran Nayak of KNF Foundation, which works with the transgender community, said that more than 20,000 persons with disabilities in Telangana had received notices, according to data seen with BLOs. Addressing the gathering, economist Parakala Prabhakar said, âEvery person who questions and dissents is a challenge to this autocratic govt.â He demanded that the SIR be scrapped, all eligible voters be restored to the rolls, and that the ECI be reconstituted through a transparent selection process. He also called for the revocation of the 2023 law granting immunity to election commissioners and the appointment of three new commissioners. âThis agitation is not against an individual but against institutional capture. We will continue until our demands are met and electoral democracy is restored,â Parakala added. title: âSri Lanka, Bangladesh happen when protests are not allowedâ: Sonam Wangchuk on anti-SIR stir crackdown
text: NEW DELHI: Activist Sonam Wangchuk on Saturday described protests as a âgreat mechanismâ for governments to improve their performance, citing the unrest in Sri Lanka and Bangladesh as examples of what could happen when demonstrations are not allowed. âNations all around the world happily permit protests, and that too right in front of Parliament. In countries like the UK, Norway and Sweden, protests are allowed right in front of Parliament,â the educationist said at an event in Mumbai. âIn India, it was far from Parliament. Even when it was just Jantar Mantar, it was too far,â he added. Wangchuk was referring to demonstrations held at Delhiâs Jantar Mantar, the capitalâs now-denotified designated protest site, in June and July following the NEET-UG paper leak in May. The protests, in which Wangchuk played a key role by undertaking an indefinite fast for over 20 days before being removed and taken to a hospital, ended with the resignation of then-Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan on July 25. His remarks came amid ongoing protests in Delhi demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. The Centre deployed extensive security measures, drawing criticism from opposition parties. âLook what happens when protests are not allowed. That is the example of Sri Lanka, Bangladesh,â Wangchuk remarked, referring to the youth- and student-led demonstrations in Sri Lanka and Bangladesh that culminated in the ouster of the incumbent governments. title: High tea after street heat: What happened at INDIA bloc meet at Rahul Gandhi's residence
text: INDIA bloc leaders gathered at Rahul's residence for high tea after four days of protest on streets NEW DELHI: INDIA bloc leaders gathered at Rahul Gandhi 's residence on Tuesday for high tea amid their ongoing protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged vote theft. They met for a high tea after four days of protest and filing a petition in SC against the CEC. From directly slamming the CEC to criticising the SIR process and criticising PM Modi and Amit Shah, several leaders including Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Supriya Sule, Tejashwi Yadav, Sanjay Raut addressed a press conference after the meet vowing to continue their protests while giving insights into what they decided at the meeting. Watch 14 Defects: Supreme Court Flags Rahul Gandhiâs Plea Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, EC | INDIA Bloc Here's what some of the key leaders said Rahul Gandhi (Congress) Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi anonunced that the INDIA bloc would continue its fight to restore the democratic process and ensure accountability for those he accused of undermining it. "We are all standing here together as one. As I said yesterday, there are no parallel protests. There is one singular protest, and the protest has one mission: restoration of democracy in India. Democracy has been destroyed in this country. The election system has been destroyed. The Constitution has been torn up and thrown away. We are fighting together to restore democratic rule, genuine democratic rule in this country." He thanked people who supported the protest and vowed to bring those responsible to justice. "It is our commitment to you that the people who have done this, Mr. Modi, Mr. Shah, Mr. Gyanesh Kumar, the lady who's hiding right now in Dehradun, and others are going to be brought to justice." "Yesterday, you saw an expression not of the political party standing here, but an expression of the people of India...We would like to thank the people of Delhi, the people of India, who stood with us against what is being done. This is not about us. This is about the people of India. This is about the future of the people of India, and we, all of us together, because we love you and we respect you, are going to fight to the end to restore the democratic process in this country. It is our commitment to you that the people who have done this, Mr. Modi, Mr. Shah, Mr. Gyanesh Kumar, the lady who's hiding right now in Dehradun, and others are going to be brought to justice," he added. Further assuring the work of the team, the Congress leader said, "I used the word 'perseverance' at the press conference yesterdayâthat this team of ours is not going to stop. Sooner or laterâwhether tomorrow, the day after, in three months, six months, a year, or two yearsâit will not stop. It will reach the end goal. I cannot tell you exactly how we will get there, because that would spoil the surprise, and we want to maintain the excitement and sense of surprise for you and the country. But I guarantee you that just as we mobilizedâwith such energy, strength, and unityâwe will continue to fight together in the same spirit. Thank you to the Supreme Courtâwe have immense respect for the Supreme Court, the Chief Justice of India, and the Indian judicial system; they have a role to play, and we hope they will play it. However, we are political people; no matter what happens, or which institution plays a role or doesn't, political resistance will continue, people's resistance will continue, and it will triumph." Mallikarjun Kharge (Congress president) The Congress president hailed INDIA bloc protests against "vote chori", CEC as "massive success". "We will carry forward this united fight (protests) against Modi govt, "vote chori", he said. D Raja (CPI general secretary) Giving highlights of what they decided in the meeting, he said, "We held a meeting with senior leaders of the INDIA bloc, where we discussed the current situation in the country and how to take forward the campaign demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar." Further slamming the decision to de ntoify Jantar Mantar as a protest site, he added, "The government has now denotified Jantar Mantar. We strongly condemn this decision. Jantar Mantar must remain a place where people can protest." MA Baby (CPM) "Gyanesh Kumar has joined the ruling party's team... He steals votes, protest site and democracy," said CPI(M) leader M A Baby after the INDIA bloc meeting . Sanjay Raut (Shiv Sena UBT "(CEC) Gyanesh Kumar is a "mafia" who has criminalised entire system; we know how to fight such mafia," he said. Further talking about the meeting, he added, "Rahul ji had convened it and invited everyoneâleaders and MPs were present for the high teaâand it was a very good meeting. Discussions were held, and everyone's suggestions regarding the way forward and their respective views were taken into account; however, the ongoing struggle against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Modi ji, and Shah ji will continueâboth in the national capital and elsewhere. " Sagarika Ghose (TMC) She accused the Election Commission of undermining free and fair elections. She demanded a halt to the SIR process, restoration of previous electoral rolls, Kumarâs removal and criminal proceedings against officials allegedly involved in electoral irregularities. "Every day, it is becoming increasingly clear that the Gyanesh Kumar-led Election Commission is undermining free and fair elections in India. As long as the Gyanesh Kumar-led Election Commission continues to function, there will be no free and fair elections in India. We stand completely united with all the leaders and parties of the INDIA alliance. We will not stop until Mr Gyanesh Kumar is removed and criminal proceedings are initiated not only against him but also against all Election Commission officials who supervised elections in Haryana, Maharashtra, Bengal and Bihar, because these have been elections marked by vote chori," she said. "The government currently in power in Bengal is illegitimate. It came to power through vote chori...We have a set of demands: halt the SIR process, stop it and revert to the old electoral rolls. Gyanesh Kumar must be dismissed, and criminal proceedings must be initiated against him. All officials, who have been involved in vote chori, must be investigated, and criminal proceedings must be initiated against them. We will not rest until this Election Commission is held accountable," she added. Supriya Sule (NCP SP) Sule expressed solidarity against the CEC and stated that their agitation will continue. "We stand united with full strength as part of the INDIA alliance; our struggle will continue because the Constitution has been undermined and is currently in danger in this country. We will persist with our agitation to uphold the rights granted to all Indians in the Constitution by Bharat Ratna Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar. A single individualârepresenting a single governmentâis making a grave mistake by attempting to trample upon these rights. We stand united with full strength to fight against this injustice and oppression; our movement will continue, from Delhi down to the grassroots level," she said. title: DMK seeks Presidential reference to SC on SIR deletions
text: Chennai: DMK president M K Stalin has urged President Droupadi Murmu to make a Presidential reference to Supreme Court under Article 143 of the Constitution, seeking its opinion on the validity of deleting 97 lakh names from Tamil Naduâs electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). In a 19-page memorandum, Stalin also sought a Presidential reference to Parliament under Article 86(2) for initiating action against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He accused Kumar of taking âillegal, unilateral, and unconstitutionalâ decisions by overriding the views of the other two election commissioners. Stalin said the deletions had disproportionately affected constituencies considered strongholds of DMK and alleged that the exercise had influenced the outcome of the assembly election. TVK won a larger share of seats where deletions were higher, he said. Noting that DMKâs objections were not an afterthought prompted by the election results, Stalin said he had opposed the exercise while serving as chief minister and had also raised concerns when reports emerged of large-scale and targeted deletion of voters in Bihar in 2025. He sought a direction to ECI that the âtainted post-SIR rollâ not be used for any future election or by-election and that the pre-SIR roll be restored, besides an independent forensic audit of the ECINET and ERONET systems. He called for measures to restore public confidence in the electoral process, including the conduct of elections through paper ballots and counting of 100% of VVPAT slips pending such a change. The memorandum follows decisions taken by DMK MPs at a meeting chaired by Stalin on Oct 17. âThis is the first and largest scam the country has ever witnessed, perpetrated by the CEC, breaching the constitutional faith and trust reposed in him,â Stalin said. Party sources said the memorandum was sent by email after a DMK delegation could not get an appointment with President till Wednesday. âThe election result in Kolathur was manipulated by deleting a large number of voters without reason to ensure that I did not win the election. These motivated deletions tilted the result in favour of the newly floated TVK,â Stalin said, expressing shock over the deletion of one lakh electors in Kolathur. He cited Tirupattur, Kanyakumari, Polur, Tirukkoilur and Paramathi-Velur, where the results were decided by narrow margins. DMK booth-level agents had assisted voters in enrolling during the SIR exercise. The final rolls, however, excluded the names of several genuine voters who had been living in their constituencies for years and had voted in previous elections, Stalin said. title: 'Because EC does not do what you say?' Chandrababu Naidu questions Jagan Reddy over 'U-turn' on CEC law
text: NEW DELHI: Andhra Pradesh chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu on Monday said his predecessor and YSRCP president YS Jagan Mohan Reddy is regretting supporting the law on Election Commission (EC) appointments because the poll body now âdoesnât do what he (Jagan) says." Addressing a press conference at his residence in Undavalli, Naidu said: âEarlier, you (Reddy) supported the procedure for appointing the CEC. But now, since the EC does not do what you say, you oppose it. Now you are talking about Gen Z... Gen Z.â Watch Delhi Protests: Foreign Hand, NGOs, UP Elections? Where's The Evidence? I Abhijit Iyer-Mitra Naidu's remarks come a day after Reddy " regretted " supporting the 2023 legislation on the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) when the YSRCP was in power in Andhra Pradesh. Under the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, which the YSRCP had supported at the time, the CEC and the two Election Commissioners are picked by a three-member committee comprising the prime minister, a Union minister and the Lok Sabha leader of the opposition. The committee recommends the names to the President, who formally appoints them. However, the legislation has come under criticism because the government, with two representatives on the committee, already has a majority in the panel. The law has been challenged in the Supreme Court. What did Jagan Mohan Reddy say After meeting the State Election Commissioner on Sunday, Jagan Mohan Reddy urged the Centre to revisit the law and expressed regret for supporting the bill in Parliament. Referring to an Indian Express report that alleged a âriftâ within the EC, with CEC Gyanesh Kumar on one side and commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi on the other, the former chief minister called for âgreater clarityâ. âRather than an exchange of allegations, the public needs clarity on what objections were recorded, what action was taken on them, and how transparently the system functioned,â he told reporters.
