title: Jantar Mantar to be prime venue for India Biennale
text: Jantar Mantar (File Photo) NEW DELHI: Within days of denotifying the area around Jantar Mantar as a protest site, the Centre has quickly moved in to select the 18th-century protected monument as one of the prime venues that will showcase exhibitions and programmes curated across over a dozen monuments and other prominent locations at âIndia Biennale 2026â that starts on Dec 4 and will be on till March 21. The first India Art, Architecture and Design Biennale was held at Red Fort in 2023 but its scale was limited. India Biennale 2026 is being called the second edition, but has been conceptualised by the culture ministry as a first of its kind in terms of scale and the ambition to bring together the best of art, architecture and design from across India and over 20 other countries. Biennale: Red Fort also among venues Nine countries, including France, Italy, Hungary, Switzerland and Sri Lanka, have already confirmed participation in âIndia Biennale 2026â. The list of monuments that will be venues for exhibitions, performances and experiences includes Purana Qila, Red Fort, Qutub Minar, Hauz Khas, Agrasen Ki Baoli, Humayunâs Tomb, Lodhi Garden, Mehrauli, Qila Rai Pithora, Safdarjung Tomb, Sabz Burj, Firozshah Kotla, Sakri Ghumti, Choti Ghumti. These are listed for now on the website and it is learnt that Jantar Mantar too will be added to the list soon. The list of venues also includes National Museum, Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts, National Gallery of Modern Art, Lalit Kala Akademi and Sangeet Natak Akademi. Sources said that the decision to use Jantar Mantar as a venue was taken after the area surrounding it was notified as a âno protestâ zone in the wake of protests for the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar. For over three decades, the astronomical observatory was the designated protest site, but its proximity to Parliament and important govt offices had long been cited as a concern. India Biennale may be among the first major events to be hosted at the venue, which is in the heart of the city with metro stations close by. The website of the Biennale introduces the vision in grand terms. âFor 108 days, Delhi monuments become the canvasâ. âFrom Dec 4 to March 21, Delhiâs heritage monuments, museums, galleries, public spaces and communities come together under a single curatorial vision,â it declares. title: 'Keep getting messages': Rahul Gandhi's big claim, and a message for CEC Gyanesh Kumar
text: Rahul's big charge against CEC (PTI photo) NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Monday levelled serious allegations against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the Narendra Modi-led Centre, claiming that around 200 government officials were in touch with the opposition and sharing information, including officials from the Enforcement Directorate (ED), Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the ministry of external affairs. Speaking at a press conference ahead of the INDIA bloc's planned march to the Supreme Court , Rahul said, "I want to tell Narendra Modi that 200 officials of your government are in touch with us and informing us, including those in the ED, CBI, foreign ministry..." Watch â200 Modi Govt Officials Informing Usâ: Rahul Gandhi's BOMBSHELL Ahead Of Supreme Court March Stepping up his attack on the poll body chief, Rahul claimed Kumar was having "sleepless nights" amid the opposition's campaign against alleged electoral irregularities. Responding to a reporter's question on whether he had communicated with the CEC, Rahul claimed that he had been "getting messages". When asked if he had a message for Gyanesh Kumar, Rahul said, "You have done a crime, and you are not the main criminal. You made a mistake and you are not the mind behind the mistake. We are after the people who are behind what you did. It is very easy for you, resign and get out of the way. We know that you have been forced by the Prime Minister, Amit Shah, Ajit Doval," Rahul Gandhi said The former Congress president also questioned why Kumar had not resigned, claiming that the opposition was receiving information from several sources. "Why is all this happening? Because we are only asking the question raised by two Election Commissioners: why is Gyanesh Kumar not resigning? These days, we are receiving information from everywhere. Gyanesh Kumar, we know your situation. We know you are unable to sleep at night, and do not worry, we will not spare you. I am telling you directly that you will not escape as Election Commissioner because of what is happening. " Rahul also accused the Centre of turning Delhi into a fortress to protect the CEC, as INDIA bloc leaders prepared to march towards the Supreme Court to demand Kumar's removal over alleged "vote chori" and concerns surrounding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. He said a public movement against alleged electoral irregularities had been under way in Delhi for the past four to five days, with protesters demanding Kumar's removal. "Since last 4-5 days, public movement is on in Delhi against 'vote chori', seeking CEC removal," the Raebareli MP said. Referring to the police action during the October 10 protests, Rahul alleged that authorities were preventing people from reaching the national capital by stopping trains and buses and forcing passengers to get off. "People are being stopped from reaching Delhi. Trains and buses are being stopped, and people are being made to get off. Delhi has been turned into a fortress, with 20,000 to 30,000 police personnel deployed everywhere. Now, think about how powerful this is. But our strategy is different," the former Congress chief said. Questioning the security arrangements, Rahul accused the government of making a "grave mistake" by protecting Kumar. He argued that the heavy police deployment would only help the opposition draw attention to its allegations against the CEC and the Centre. "We want 20,000 to 30,000 police personnel deployed on the streets. " Rahul further claimed that some police personnel supported the opposition's campaign and wanted it to continue. "I am happy to tell you that 50% of the police personnel, and I am counting them, are telling us that what you are doing is right and that we should continue..." title: SFI activist alleges assault by party colleagues, says threatened with fate of Siddharthan
text: K ozhikode: SFI Wayanad district joint secretary Sayanth has publicly accused the organisationâs district secretary Adarsh and central committee member Sandra Ravindran of assaulting him at the party area committee office in Pulpally, alleging that he was beaten with a microphone stand and a steel rod. title: 'Your social media posts amounted to instigation': Bombay HC pulls up actor Imran Khan - top quotes
text: 'Your social media posts amounted to instigation': Bombay HC told actor Imran Khan. NEW DELHI: The Bombay high court on Monday pulled up actor Imran Khan, a US citizen holding an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card, for taking part in a protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The court observed that the right to protest was available only to Indian citizens, after which the actor tendered an unconditional apology. A bench comprising Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna remarked that instead of deporting Khan immediately, authorities had shown leniency by issuing him a notice asking him to leave the country. Khan's lawyer, Venkatesh Dhond, responded by submitting an undertaking that the 43-year-old actor would not participate in any protest in the future. He also conveyed Khan's unconditional apology to the court. The actor had approached the high court challenging a notice issued by the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO), directing him to leave India by October 28. The notice followed his participation in a protest over the SIR exercise in Mumbai last month. The bench posted the matter for further hearing on December 7 and extended its earlier order keeping the FRRO notice in abeyance until then. The court also reiterated that an OCI cardholder does not have the right to participate in protests in India. Here's what court said: "If an Indian had done the same thing elsewhere would it have been tolerated? If this had happened in America, the person would have been put on the next flight back to India," the high court remarked, suggesting Khan to consider taking Indian citizenship if he was so keen on participating in protests. The court said while it was not disputing the powers of the authorities to take such an action (to issue notice), certain ground realities also need to be considered. "He (Khan) is ready to tender an unconditional apology. He has been in India since childhood. Show some magnanimity and a big heart now. We have to be 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' (the world is one family)," the court said. As far as law is concerned, the authorities have sovereign powers, the court said, adding they would be well within their powers to deport the actor. "As an OCI cardholder, you (Khan) are at the mercy of this country. Hence, such behaviour cannot be tolerated, but one chance can be given," the high court said. For what had he (Khan) gone to a place of protest (in Mumbai)? the bench asked while adding in a lighter vein that the actor does not even have any film coming up to promote. "The rights Indian citizens enjoy and the rights available to OCI cardholders are different. If he had been an Indian citizen then the situation would have been different," Chief Justice Tripathi noted . Khan holds an OCI card and hence he cannot behave like an Indian citizen, the bench further said. "You (Khan) had no right to participate in a protest of such nature. You have no connection with the SIR (Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls undertaken by EC). The right to protest is not available to an OCI cardholder," HC said. Senior counsel Venkatesh Dhond, appearing for Khan, initially submitted an undertaking to the court on the actor's behalf, assuring that he would neither participate in any future protest nor instigate others to do so. However, the court said the undertaking alone would not be enough and asked Khan to tender an unconditional apology. The court observed that Khan had been in India since childhood, had worked in the film industry here and had earned recognition in the country. "Your social media posts (after he was released from detention by police) amounted to instigation. You have young followers who are bound to get influenced," it said. title: Cabinet secretariat merely acknowledged complaint of ECs against senior poll officer: RTI
text: The two ECs alleged the changes were made without prior discussion with the commission or officers concerned. NEW DELHI: After election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi wrote to cabinet secretary TV Somanathan in July objecting to the revised allocation of work among senior commission officers by senior deputy Election Commissioner (DEC) Maneesh Garg without EC approval, the secretariat merely sent them an acknowledgement with a copy to CEC Gyanesh Kumar for information, an RTI reply has revealed. The senior officers among whom the work was reallocated by Garg, who was only filling in for DEC (administration) Bhanu Prakash Yeturu while he was on leave, included Seema Khanna, who was brought in as head of the IT division of EC. Sandhu and Joshi, according to a report in Indian Express dated Sept 23, had in internal notes to DEC concerned, alleged that the ECINET software conceived and managed by the IT division, was too centralised, blocking access to field officers who were authorised by law to make changes to the electoral roll. Watch EC Makes 4 Changes To SSR Amid Anti-CEC Protests; Congress Says âToo Little, Too Lateâ Explaining the rationale behind the reluctance to take any action, a confidential note on the file shared by the Cabinet secretariat with transparency activist, Commodore Lokesh K Batra (Retd), as part of its 21-page RTI reply, stated that EC being a Constitutional body is insulated from the Executive's interference by design. "The...communications are from the ECs in their individual capacity and, while they must be taken with due seriousness, they cannot be seen as a formal communication from the commission as a whole," it said adding that Garg is an officer of the EC and his work and conduct is to be regulated by rules and guidelines of EC. "In the absence of any official communication from the commission as a whole, any action at this stage may be inappropriate. It may also be construed as interference in the functioning of the constitutional body," the note underlines before announcing the decision to merely send an acknowledgement to the two ECs, with copies marked to the CEC and the DoPT. Commodore Batra had on September 24 sought copies of the Commissioners' communications, details of the steps taken by the Cabinet Secretariat and the relevant file notings. This was a day after The Indian Express reported that two election commissioners had objected on record 14 times in 10 months to steps involving the addition of new voters and deletion of names from electoral rolls, and had approached the Cabinet Secretary over concerns about the integrity of the voter database. According to the documents shared as part of the RTI response, the two ECs Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, wrote separate but near-identical letters to Cabinet Secretary TV Somanathan on July 29, 2026, objecting to the conduct of a Garg and an order he issued revising the allocation of work among senior officers. The two Commissioners alleged that the changes were made without prior discussion with the Commission or the officers concerned. A cabinet secretariat file noting dated Aug 3 says that both the ECs have stated that Garg, after assuming the charge as link officer of DEC (Administration), has issued an order regarding work allocation of equivalent and senior officers to him without discussing the revised work allocation with the Commission or the officers concerned. âFurther, the ECs stated that this has happened despite repeated oral and written instructions to all concerned officers against taking such actions without prior discussion/approval of the Commission,â noting highlights. âIn this connection, we may request the CEC for his opinion on the issue," it said. In another noting dated Aug 4, it is stated that the EC is a âConstitutional body and is insulated from executive interference by design to ensure that it functions independently and in a transparent manner. The working and functioning of the Commission are governed by the rules and guidelines of the Election Commission.â It further states that since the communications are from the ECs in their individual capacity and, while they must be taken with due seriousness, they cannot be seen as a formal communication from the Commission as a whole. Calling West Bengal a victim of the circumstances surrounding the SIR exercise, Mamata said her party would continue to resist what she described as an attempt to undermine the state's electoral rights. Called by Left organisations, the march drew NSUI members, the All India Studentsâ Association (AISA) and the Revolutionary Youth Association (RYA). title: 10 lakh turnout target, 4,000 cops, 200 CCTV: Delhi braces for INDIA bloc's anti-CEC rally at Ramlila Maidan
text: Preparations underway at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan for the INDIA bloc's anti-CEC rally NEW DELHI: Delhi is gearing up for INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on Sunday, with opposition parties expecting a turnout of up to 10 lakh people and police deploying more than 4,000 personnel to manage security and crowds. The rally is being organised to protest against alleged electoral irregularities and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The mobilisation comes amid the Opposition's allegations of 'vote chori' and large-scale voter deletions during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Watch âGyanesh Wonât Survive As CECâ: Rahul Gandhiâs BIG Warning At Mock Impeachment 'Chalo Dilli' march to precede rally The programme will begin with a march, called 'Chalo Dilli', from the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction to Ramlila Maidan at noon. The rally at the venue is scheduled to continue from 10am to 5pm. INDIA bloc leaders are expected to travel in open buses from Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence to the march's starting point. The protest is expected to bring together leaders and supporters of opposition parties, along with student groups and civil society organisations. The INDIA bloc has appealed to students, youth, women and workers to participate. The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), founded by Abhijeet Dipke, and several student organisations have also extended support to the mobilisation. 4,000 cops, 200 CCTV cameras for security While INDIA bloc leaders have projected a turnout of up to 10 lakh, Delhi Police expects around 50,000 people. Officials estimate that the ground can accommodate 45,000 to 50,000 people when empty, news agency PTI reported. With chairs, enclosures and passageways in place, its capacity is expected to fall to around 30,000 to 40,000. Additional space will be kept outside to manage any spillover. More than 4,000 police personnel, along with Central Armed Police Forces companies, will be deployed along the march route and at the venue. Ramlila Maidan has been divided into 14 security zones, each supervised by an assistant commissioner of police-rank officer. More than 200 CCTV cameras, drones and body-worn cameras will be used for surveillance. A control room has also been set up inside the ground to monitor the arrangements. Traffic curbs across key Delhi roads Traffic restrictions will remain in force across parts of Delhi between 10am and 5pm. Diversions are planned at major intersections, including ITO, Delhi Gate, Rajghat, Ajmeri Gate and Turkman Gate. Commuters have been advised to avoid Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg, Jawaharlal Nehru Marg, Minto Road and Desh Bandhu Gupta Road. Special arrangements will be made to ensure that ambulances and emergency vehicles can reach LNJP and GB Pant hospitals. Passengers travelling to New Delhi Railway Station have also been advised to plan their journeys in advance. Delhi Police has said permission has been granted for the rally at Ramlila Maidan, but it has not received an application for the proposed procession from the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction. title: 'India not a banana republic': BJP attacks Rahul Gandhi ahead of INDIA bloc rally
text: BJP targets Rahul Gandhi over INDIA bloc rally, alleges bid to create unrest NEW DELHI: Union minister JP Nadda on Sunday launched a sharp attack on the Congress and Rahul Gandhi over the INDIA bloc's rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, accusing the opposition of using the banner of democracy to create unrest, damage the economy and destabilise an elected government. Reacting to the 'Chalo Delhi' mobilisation, Nadda said the rally was a âcalculated conspiracy to plunge the nation into anarchyâin the name of democracyâ. He described it as a âfoolish, orchestrated dramaâ by parties that had been defeated and rejected by voters. Nadda further said that it will prove to be the final "nail in the coffin" of Congress' "political downfall". Watch JP Nadda Calls INDIA Bloc Rally A âConspiracyâ To Create Anarchy, Targets Rahul Gandhi Addressing Rahul Gandhi directly, the Union minister outlined what he called the Congress leader's model of politics, alleging that it involved spreading misinformation, provoking street protests, harming the economy and seeking to destabilise an elected government at the behest of foreign powers. âThe first stage is spreading lies and rumours; the second is inciting anarchy and chaos on the streets; the third is damaging the nationâs economy; and the fourth is attempting to destabilise an elected government at the behest of foreign powers,â Nadda said. He also alleged that the November 1 rally had four specific objectives: hurting the sentiments of the Sikh community, triggering violence in Delhi to bring down a democratically elected government, affecting the earnings of traders during the festive season and damaging India's reputation. Nadda's remarks came amid the INDIA bloc's protest against alleged irregularities in the revision of electoral rolls and its demand for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. "Rahul Gandhi, listen carefully: this is Indiaânot some 'banana republic' where you can incite arson, trigger riots, or push an agenda for 'regime change' whenever you please. Stop dreaming, Rahul Gandhi. India is the worldâs oldest and most robust democracy. November 1st stands as the most infamous and darkest stain in Indiaâs democratic history. On this very day, goons nurtured by the Congress party massacred our innocent Sikh brethren. Thousands of Sikh families were rendered homeless overnight, and thousands of women were widowed. The nation has not forgotten; even today, the 'Widow Colony' in Delhi bears witness to that horrific and bloody chapter of Congress history. To this day, the Gandhi family has not offered a sincere apology to the Sikh community for that grave sin. Observe the insensitivity of the Congress and the petty mindset of Rahul Gandhi. On this dark dayâa day when the nation ought to be remembering its martyrs and victimsâRahul Gandhi stands at Ramlila Maidan, seeking only to further his own political agenda ...", Nadda added. BJP accuses Opposition of disrupting peace and business The rally has also drawn criticism from the BJP over its timing, with the ruling party accusing Congress of holding a political event on the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots. BJP is holding a separate march in West Delhi under the banner of remembering the victims of the 1984 violence. The march is scheduled to proceed from Hari Nagar Bus Depot to Tilak Nagar Metro Station, with Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri, Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta, Delhi BJP president and other party leaders expected to participate. Meanwhile, the BJP and its Mahayuti allies held a 'Lokshahi Bachao, Anarajakta Hatao' (Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy) padyatra in Mumbai on Sunday. Maharashtra BJP president Ravindra Chavan accused the Congress of spreading what he described as false narratives about constitutional institutions, including the judiciary and Parliament. âAt a time when the entire nation is witnessing a phase of development-oriented governance under the leadership of PM Modi, the opposition Congress party is, without any valid reason, attempting to create confusion among the public by propagating false narratives about our established institutions,â Chavan said. Shiv Sena MP Naresh Mhaske also criticised Rahul Gandhi and his associates, alleging that their activities were against the Constitution. BJP has also launched a nationwide 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' campaign to counter opposition allegations relating to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Party workers are expected to reach villages and households to present the BJP's position on the electoral process. INDIA bloc leaders allege voter irregularities, restrictions on rally supporters The opposition alliance, meanwhile, has maintained that its mobilisation is aimed at protecting democratic rights and raising concerns over alleged deletions of legitimate voters from electoral rolls. Himachal Pradesh deputy chief minister Mukesh Agnihotri alleged that buses carrying supporters from his state were being stopped at different points on their way to Delhi. He claimed that some vehicles were intercepted over pollution norms and others over taxation issues, despite the buses being BS-VI-compliant. âWe had already instructed everyone that such obstructions might occur, and if stopped, they should simply continue on foot to reach Himachal Bhawan,â Agnihotri said, adding that the supporters were prepared to walk to Ramlila Maidan. Himachal Pradesh minister Vikramaditya Singh called for accountability from Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and claimed that the number of votes involved in the alleged irregularities had risen from 13 crore to around 16 crore. âI am confident that, in the near future, the CEC Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign, and a new revolution will sweep across the entire country,â Singh said. Uttarakhand leader of opposition Yashpal Arya described the rally as a âbattle for justiceâ to protect democracy and the Constitution. Congress leader Kunwar Danish Ali also called the mobilisation historic and accused the government of targeting students, young people and farmers. The INDIA bloc has demanded the replacement of electronic voting machines with paper ballots and the immediate resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner. Rahul Gandhi had appealed to people in Delhi and neighbouring states to join the march, either from Connaught Place or directly at Ramlila Maidan. Heavy security arrangements across Delhi Security has been tightened across the national capital in view of the two political events. Nearly 10,000 police and paramilitary personnel, including Delhi Police, Central Armed Police Forces, the CRPF and Rapid Action Force, have been deployed across Central and New Delhi, ANI reported. More than 4,000 personnel have been stationed around Ramlila Maidan, along the route from Minto Bridge and in surrounding areas. Barricades have also been placed around Connaught Place, Jantar Mantar, Bhagwan Das Road and areas near the Supreme Court and the Election Commission's office. title: Imran Khan apologises as Bombay High Court slams the actor for participating in protests despite being an OCI card holder: 'If an Indian had done the same thing elsewhere would it have been tolerated?'
text: The Bombay High Court on Monday pulled up actor Imran Khan , a US citizen holding an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card, for participating in a protest related to the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC)-Special Intensive Revision (SIR) issue in Mumbai. The court observed that the fundamental right to protest is reserved for Indian citizens, following which the actor tendered an unconditional apology and assured the bench that he would not participate in any such demonstration in the future. A bench comprising Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna observed that India's magnanimity was evident from the fact that Khan, despite being a US citizen, was first served a notice asking him to leave the country rather than being deported immediately. Watch Imran Khan Receives October 28 Deadline to Leave India After Joining Mumbaiâs CJP Protest Appearing for Khan, senior advocate Venkatesh Dhond promptly submitted an undertaking on behalf of the 43-year-old actor, assuring the court that he would neither participate in protests in the future nor encourage anyone else to do so. He also tendered an unconditional apology. The court subsequently scheduled Khan's petition challenging the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) notice for further hearing on December 7. The notice had directed him to leave India by October 28 over his alleged participation in a demonstration against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in Mumbai last month. The bench also extended its earlier order keeping the FRRO notice in abeyance until the next hearing. During the proceedings, the court maintained that an OCI cardholder does not enjoy the same rights as an Indian citizen, particularly when it comes to participating in protests. Drawing a comparison with how foreign nationals are treated in other countries, the bench remarked, "If an Indian had done the same thing elsewhere would it have been tolerated? If this had happened in America, the person would have been put on the next flight back to India," The judges also suggested that Khan consider applying for Indian citizenship if he wished to participate in demonstrations concerning issues affecting Indian citizens. While the bench acknowledged that the authorities were within their sovereign powers to issue the notice, it also urged them to consider the circumstances before taking further action. "He (Khan) is ready to tender an unconditional apology. He has been in India since childhood. Show some magnanimity and a big heart now. We have to be 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' (the world is one family)," the court observed. At the same time, the judges made it clear that the actor could not take his OCI status for granted. Referring to the powers available to the government under the law, the bench said, "As an OCI cardholder, you (Khan) are at the mercy of this country. Hence, such behaviour cannot be tolerated, but one chance can be given," the HC said. The court also questioned Khan's reason for attending a demonstration concerning an issue linked to Indian electoral processes. Asking what connection the actor had with the SIR exercise, the bench remarked that he had no right to participate in a protest concerning Indian citizens. "For what had he (Khan) gone to a place of protest (in Mumbai)?" the judges asked, adding in a lighter vein that the actor did not even have an upcoming film to promote. "The rights Indian citizens enjoy and the rights available to OCI cardholders are different. If he had been an Indian citizen then the situation would have been different," Chief Justice Tripathi noted. Reiterating its position, the bench added that Khan's OCI status did not entitle him to exercise the same privileges as an Indian citizen. "You (Khan) had no right to participate in a protest of such nature. You have no connection with the SIR (Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls undertaken by EC). The right to protest is not available to an OCI cardholder," the HC said. The judges further took note of Khan's social media activity following his release from police detention, observing that his posts could influence his young followers. "Your social media posts (after he was released from detention by police) amounted to instigation. You have young followers who are bound to get influenced," the court said. The FRRO issued the 'Leave India' notice under Sections 7(2)(C) and 29 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, provisions that empower the government to regulate the movement of foreign nationals and order their removal from the country. Khan was directed to leave India by October 28, failing which deportation proceedings could be initiated. The action followed his brief detention by Mumbai Police during a demonstration held on October 10 at the city's historic August Kranti Maidan. The protest was organised in solidarity with an agitation by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which had demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the SIR of electoral rolls. In his petition challenging the FRRO's decision, filed through advocate Zulfiquar Memon, Khan maintained that he had neither participated in the gathering nor had any association or affiliation with its organisers. Describing the notice as "illegal, arbitrary, perverse and drastic," the actor alleged that the authorities had failed to apply their minds before targeting him because of his public profile. He further argued that the action amounted to "patent non-application of mind and the arbitrary targeting" of a public figure. The petition also contended, "Not only is the notice manifestly disproportionate, if implemented, it would reduce the very principles of natural justice that the authorities are duty-bound to uphold, to nothing but a dead letter." title: âSave democracy, remove anarchyâ: BJP marches in Chandni Chowk as Congress readies November 1 rally, and traders count the cost
text: The Congress is planning a large rally amid escalating tensions with the BJP over electoral issues NEW DELHI: In a political face-off where both sides claim to be defending democracy, Delhiâs traders are caught worrying about their Diwali business. As the Congress prepares to bring its âvote choriâ campaign to Ramlila Maidan on November 1, the BJP has taken the battle to the streets of Old Delhi, leading a âSave Democracy, Remove Anarchyâ padyatra in Chandni Chowk and sharpening its attack on Rahul Gandhi. Led by BJP president Nitin Nabin and CM Rekha Gupta, the march comes amid mounting opposition from traders who fear that barricading, traffic diversions and possible metro restrictions during the festive shopping season could disrupt business across the capitalâs major wholesale markets. The political temperature has risen further after Rahul Gandhi challenged traders to ask Prime Minister Narendra Modi to remove chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The result is a three-way confrontation: the BJP accuses Congress of creating disorder, the opposition alleges electoral irregularities and demands accountability from the poll chief, while traders insist that their livelihoods should not become collateral damage in the political showdown. âDemocracy is in safe handsâ: BJP turns fire on Rahul Gandhi At the Chandni Chowk padyatra, BJP president Nitin Nabin defended Prime Minister Narendra Modiâs leadership and questioned Rahul Gandhiâs commitment to the Constitution. âDemocracy is in safe hands,â Nabin said, asserting that people had faith in Modi and that the Prime Minister enjoyed the mandate of the countryâs 140 crore people. Targeting the Congress leaderâs frequent references to the Constitution, Nabin alleged that Gandhi carried a copy of the document without genuinely caring about it. He also predicted that the Congress would be politically wiped out if its leaders continued to follow Gandhiâs leadership. Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta joined the attack, ridiculing the Congressâs âvote choriâ slogan and describing its political campaigns as repeated attempts to launch a leader whose initiatives, she claimed, failed to gain traction. Rekha Gupta said people knew where they had voted and who had won, adding that the public continued to repose faith in the Central Government and Modi. 'Holding Delhi hostage' A day earlier, Delhi BJP president Harsh Malhotra accused the Congress of repeatedly disrupting normal life in the capital through protests, including demonstrations near Parliament and the Supreme Court. Malhotra said the party was organising the padyatra against what it described as the âanarchist behaviourâ of Rahul Gandhi and the Congress. As per news agency ANI, the BJPâs campaign comes as the Congress prepares for an impeachment-style public proceeding against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on October 30, followed by a âDilli Chaloâ march and a public gathering at Ramlila Maidan on November 1. The proposed gathering is intended to intensify pressure on the government over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the oppositionâs demand for the CECâs resignation. The BJP, however, has made the likely disruption to Delhiâs festive-season commerce a central part of its political counterattack. Rahul Gandhiâs '30-second' challenge Rahul Gandhi has pushed back against the criticism, arguing that the restrictions affecting Delhiâs markets are the result of government-imposed security arrangements rather than the oppositionâs protests. In a post on X, Gandhi said the government had shut metro services, sealed roads and effectively locked down parts of the capital. He linked these restrictions to the oppositionâs allegation of electoral malpractice and called on traders to demand the removal of Gyanesh Kumar. âTell Modi to sack accused no. 4, Gyanesh Kumar and the protests will stop in 30 seconds,â Gandhi wrote. The remark has added another layer to the dispute. While traders are asking Congress to postpone its rally until after Diwali, Gandhi has sought to redirect their anger towards the government, arguing that action against the CEC would bring the protests to an end. Business community sounds alarm The political exchange comes against the backdrop of an increasingly vocal protest by Delhiâs trading community. On Monday, traders staged a demonstration at Kashmere Gate, urging the Congress to defer its November 1 rally until after Diwali. They also wrote to Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, asking the party to reschedule the gathering. The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) said the anticipated crowd, security arrangements, traffic diversions and possible restrictions on public transport could hit business across major wholesale markets. The traders raised the slogan: â20,000 traders have one appeal: hold the rally after Diwali.â CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said the Congress had indicated that around 10 lakh people could attend the rally, while the actual capacity of Ramlila Maidan was approximately 50,000, according to his claim reported by PTI. Goyal warned that the scale of the expected gathering could affect more than 20 major wholesale hubs within a five-kilometre radius of the venue. These include Chandni Chowk, Sadar Bazar, Khari Baoli, Naya Bazar, Chawri Bazar, Daryaganj and Kashmere Gate. He also claimed that traffic restrictions could prevent three to four lakh buyers from outside Delhi, who visit the capital daily, from reaching the markets. The CTI said it would write to leaders of all parties in the INDIA bloc, urging them to consider the concerns of traders and postpone the rally. Traders fear a festive-season hit worth crores For Delhiâs wholesale traders, the timing is particularly sensitive. The period leading up to Dhanteras, Diwali and Bhai Dooj is a crucial phase for sales, with buyers travelling from Delhi and other states to purchase goods in bulk. Paramjeet Singh Pamma, president of the Sadar Bazar Bari Market Trade Association, also appealed to the Congress leadership to postpone the event, warning that traffic restrictions and difficulties accessing wholesale markets could lead to losses worth crores of rupees. The tradersâ concerns are not limited to the November 1 gathering. Goyal told PTI that a gathering of around 2,000 to 4,000 people at Jantar Mantar on October 10 had, according to his account, resulted in metro station closures, barricading and restrictions that forced more than 20 major markets to shut. That claim has become part of the tradersâ argument for rescheduling the rally. Their demand is not necessarily a rejection of the oppositionâs right to protest. Rather, they want the demonstration moved to a date when the economic consequences for businesses are likely to be lower. Congress leader counters tradersâ objections Congress leader Sandeep Dikshit questioned the argument that the rally would cause widespread damage to Delhiâs trade. Dikshit said the event was confined to a specific area and argued that a large gathering could also generate business for street vendors, food sellers and small shopkeepers. He asked why the interests of roadside vendors and other informal traders should be ignored when assessing the economic impact of a political rally. âStop sycophancyâ: Congress leaderâs remarks add fuel The dispute has also triggered a sharp exchange over the business communityâs relationship with the government. As per an ANI report, Congress leader Hussain Dalwai urged traders not to support the government unconditionally and instead pressure it over alleged electoral irregularities. "The business community should stop sycophancy towards the government and instead exert pressure on the government. The way the government is functioning, it is the right of the people to protest now. And why do people protest? Do they protest just like that? Do they do it to cause trouble to the business community? Everyone has the right to vote in the elections, but this very right has been snatched away to prove a point. The rights of 13 crore people have been stripped away, and the business community should speak up about this. If you want to exert pressure, bring it upon the government. You are the ones who brought this government to power; now pull it down,â he said. title: 'PM Modi, Amit Shah suffering loss': Sanjay Raut on business concerns of traders ahead of INDIA bloc rally
text: File photo: Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut on Sunday dismissed concerns that the INDIA bloc's rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan would disrupt business in the national capital, taking a swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah by calling them the country's âonly two tradersâ. Speaking to news agency ANI ahead of the opposition alliance's 'Chalo Delhi' mobilisation, Raut said any losses suffered by the two leaders as a result of the demonstration would be acceptable. Watch âModi Hatao, Democracy Bachaoâ: Kharge Leads INDIA Bloc Attack On BJP Over âVote Choriâ Claims Today He also claimed that lakhs of people were travelling to Delhi to demand a change of government and defend constitutional democracy. âThere are no real concerns among the traders; in this country, the only two 'traders' are Modi ji and Shah ji. They are certainly suffering losses. If such movements cause them losses, then so be it,â Raut said. He described the mobilisation as a show of national strength rather than an event organised by any one political party, claiming that attempts to prevent people from reaching the capital would only increase the size of the gathering. âLakhs of people are arriving. There are significant attempts to stop them, but the more they try to block people, the larger the crowd will grow. People will break through all the barricades to get here. They want a regime change. They do not want this govt,â he said. Raut added that such programmes would continue to be held in Delhi in front of the Prime Minister and the home minister. Raut accuses Election Commission of surrendering autonomy The Shiv Sena (UBT) leader also accused the Election Commission of India (ECI) of functioning under pressure from the ruling establishment, alleging that constitutional institutions had failed to maintain their independence. âConstitutional watchdogs have surrendered their autonomy. When votes are manipulated, and institutions turn a blind eye, the people of the country have no option but to demand accountability out in the open. We will not allow the Election Commission to become a front organisation for the ruling party,â he said. Raut maintained that the INDIA bloc remained united in its opposition to alleged voter roll tampering and what it described as the suppression of democratic norms. âThis massive mobilisation is a loud and clear message to the government: you cannot govern this country through fear, misuse of agencies, and electoral manipulation. The voice of the people will triumph,â he added. Backing the rally, Samajwadi Party leader S T Hasan told ANI that the demonstration could become âhistoricâ if the government allowed it to proceed without interference. The former MP said the mobilisation was aimed at protecting the Constitution and democratic values. âIf the government doesnât interfere and allows the rally to take place, it is set to be a historic one. This rally is about saving the nation, protecting the Constitution, and safeguarding our democracy,â Hasan said. He also expressed concern over what he described as a decline in the global perception of India's electoral integrity, claiming that the country was increasingly being viewed as a âpseudo-democracyâ. âThe message currently circulating globally is that the worldâs largest democracy has effectively become a 'pseudo-democracy', a place where votes are stolen, fair elections do not occur, and the principle of 'might is right' prevails,â he said. Hasan urged citizens to support the opposition's initiative, saying it was the duty of every Indian to stand up for the country and protect democracy. INDIA bloc expects large turnout at Ramlila Maidan The remarks came as supporters of INDIA bloc parties began gathering at Ramlila Maidan and other locations in Delhi on Sunday morning for the 'Chalo Delhi' rally against alleged electoral irregularities. The opposition alliance is also demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Congress supporters assembled outside Himachal Bhawan, while Samajwadi Party workers gathered near party chief Akhilesh Yadav's residence before proceeding towards the rally venue. Party workers from several states had also reached the capital on Saturday or earlier. The march is scheduled to begin at noon from the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction and culminate at Ramlila Maidan. Senior opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi , Mallikarjun Kharge, Mamata Banerjee, Abhishek Banerjee, Hemant Soren, Revanth Reddy, Tejashwi Yadav and Akhilesh Yadav, are expected to attend. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had urged people travelling to Delhi for the protest to also shop from local traders ahead of Diwali, Chhath and Bhai Dooj. In a video message posted on X on Saturday, he said the opposition's programme would not hurt businesses and asked supporters to combine their participation in the rally with some shopping. The INDIA bloc has estimated that up to 10 lakh people could attend the mobilisation, while Delhi Police expects a turnout of around 50,000. Ramlila Maidan can accommodate 45,000 to 50,000 people when empty, but the estimated capacity is lower â around 30,000 to 40,000 â with chairs, enclosures and passageways in place. title: INDIA bloc huddle: Leaders to meet virtually on CEC row; SIR irregularities on agenda
text: INDIA bloc leaders to meet today to discuss strategy against CEC Gyanesh Kumar NEW DELHI: Leaders of the INDIA bloc will meet through video conferencing on Thursday evening to discuss their strategy over the ongoing row involving chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, sources cited by news agency ANI said, with Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge set to chair the meeting. The meeting comes as Opposition parties continue their campaign against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demand accountability from the Election Commission of India (ECI). Watch Delhi Showdown: Rahul Gandhi To Lead INDIA Bloc March To SC Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar The opposition has accused the poll panel of facilitating the deletion of eligible voters from electoral rolls and has sought Kumarâs resignation. The Election Commission has maintained that it follows established procedures and defended its role in conducting elections. Opposition steps up campaign against Election Commission The INDIA bloc had earlier announced a joint action plan under its âSave Democracyâ campaign. The proposed programme included protests, a march towards the Election Commission headquarters and a rally in New Delhi on November 1. On October 6, INDIA bloc MPs led by Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi marched towards Nirvachan Sadan, the Election Commissionâs headquarters, seeking a meeting with the poll panel. Delhi Police stopped the march amid heavy barricading and detained several opposition leaders, including Rahul Gandhi and Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra. They were later released. Following the protest, the ECI said Delhi Police had informed it that a delegation of around 240 MPs wanted to meet the Election Commissioners and submit a memorandum at the Parliament House Annexe. The poll panel described the proposed venue and manner of seeking the meeting as âunusualâ under its established protocol. Delhi Police said the march had not been granted permission and cited prohibitory orders to explain its action against the protesters. The opposition subsequently approached President Droupadi Murmu. An INDIA bloc delegation, including Rahul Gandhi, Kharge, Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee and Samajwadi Party representatives, submitted a memorandum outlining its demands on October 9. The memorandum sought Kumarâs resignation, suspension of the SIR exercise, restoration of voters allegedly deleted from electoral rolls and a return to paper ballots. The opposition also called for the repeal of the 2023 law granting immunity to the chief election commissioner and other election commissioners for official duties. Kharge targets immunity law, EVMs On Wednesday, Kharge accused the BJP-led government of undermining democratic institutions and shielding election officials from accountability. He said the oppositionâs campaign was aimed at protecting the Constitution and democracy rather than securing electoral gains for any particular party. Kharge criticised Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, which grants legal immunity to current and former Election Commissioners for official duties. He argued that the provision protected election officials from accountability and demanded its repeal. âWe are asking the BJP to repeal that law. Because you are giving protection to the Election Commissioner and letting him make mistakes. And whatever mistakes have happened today, they happened through Gyanesh Kumar. Why did you give him immunity? It was given so that you can make mistakes through him just by telling him to do so, and forgive him. The Chief Justice doesnât have immunity. The President of India doesnât have it. An Election Commissioner does,â Kharge said. He also called for Kumarâs removal, the scrapping of electronic voting machines (EVMs) and a return to paper ballots, while demanding stricter checks on changes to voter lists. âFollow the constitutional system, and remove Gyanesh Kumar, whom you have appointed today. Along with removing him, change the system too. Bring the previous law back, get rid of the EVMs, bring back ballot papers, and the software that sits in one place and controls the whole country. Stop using BLOs to make changes to the voter list,â he said. Kharge also criticised the governmentâs response to opposition concerns, alleging that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah were using ministers and constitutional officials to avoid directly addressing the issues raised by the opposition. INDIA bloc challenges SIR, Jantar Mantar decision At a meeting on October 13, INDIA bloc leaders reiterated their resolve to continue the campaign and said they would challenge the denotification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. title: Congress to hold âVote Bachao' rally at Ramlila Maidan on Nov 1; Amit Shah to lead padayatra in T'gana on Nov 2
text: Congress will hold âvote bachao, desh bachaoâ rally on Nov 1 in Delhi, while Amit Shah will attend the âloktantra bachao, arajakta hataoâ padayatra on Nov 2 in Telangana NEW DELHI: The Congress will hold a âVote Bachao, Desh Bachaoâ mega rally at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi on November 1, party president Mallikarjun Kharge said on Monday. The protest comes over the alleged vote theft, demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and an immediate halt of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). Meanwhile, Union home minister Amit Shah is also set to attend a BJP foot march in Telangana a day later, on November 2, to counter what the party calls the Congress's âfalse narrativeâ against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Telangana BJP president N Ramchander Rao announced Shah's participation in the November 2 âLoktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hataoâ (save democracy, remove anarchy) padayatra on Monday. The announcement comes amid a political row over the SIR exercise, with the Congress accusing the Election Commission of large-scale electoral irregularities. âThey (Congress) are trying to create anarchy in the state and country. That's why we are going to organise a padayatra with the theme 'Loktantra Bachao - Arajakta Hatao' (save democracy - remove anarchy) . Amit Shah ji will attend the padayatra on 2nd (of November),â news agency PTI reported, quoting Rao. Kharge announces mega rally at Ramleela Maidan Kharge announced the November 1 rally in a video shared on X, alleging that the constitutional right to vote of millions of Indians was under threat. âThe constitutional right of the Indian people to cast their votes is under threat. CEC Gyanesh Kumar is solely responsible for this; he has acted entirely at the behest of the Prime Minister and the Home Minister,â Kharge said. Kharge also criticised the government over inflation. In his video address, he said, âGreetings, friends. It is the festive season, yet you are currently grappling with back-breaking inflation. The government, however, is completely unconcernedâall they know how to do is steal votes. Large-scale vote theft has taken place, and it continues even now.â Announcing the rally, he said, âIn this regard, a 'Save the Vote, Save the Nation' (Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao) mega-rally will be held on November 1st at the historic Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi.â âI appeal to you to participate actively in this rally to protect our Constitution and democracy, and to help make this campaign a success. Long live the Constitution! Jai Hind!â he added. BJP challenges Congress over SIR claims Rao accused the Congress of spreading misinformation about the electoral roll revision and challenged Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy to identify voters whose names had been wrongly deleted. Observing that Congress was spreading lies over the SIR exercise, Rao said he was ready to visit the chief minister's native village, Kondareddypalle, to check how many voters' names had been removed from the rolls. He said genuine voters whose names were deleted had the option of getting them included again. Rao also asked Congress ministers in Telangana to identify at least 10 voters whose names had been deleted and explain the reasons for their removal. Responding to allegations that 13 crore voters had been removed during the SIR exercise, Rao claimed that they fell into the categories of 'Absent, Shifted, Dead and Duplicate' (ASDD). Of these, he claimed, 2.8 crore were dead, three crore were absent or untraceable when booth-level officers visited them, 6.3 crore had permanently shifted and nearly one crore names were registered at multiple locations. He cited the example of a man in Hyderabad who had admitted to having voter registrations at three places. Rao targets Kharge, Congress over rally Rao also criticised Kharge over his remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi, alleging that Congress was unable to accept that a 'chaiwala' had become the country's Prime Minister. He said the party was desperate to return to power after losing elections since 2014. The Telangana BJP president asked party workers to burn Congress effigies at district headquarters on Monday in protest against Kharge's remarks. He also took exception to Congress leaders from Telangana travelling to Delhi for the November 1 rally, citing water shortages in the state. Rao claimed that more than 300 of Telangana's over 600 mandals were facing drought-like conditions due to a rainfall deficit. title: Cong, CJP & Left rally in solidarity with Delhi protests
text: Nagpur: The Indian National Congress , along with the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and other organisations like the CPI-affiliated All India Student Association (AISA), took to the streets on Wednesday in solidarity with the protests currently underway in New Delhi, calling for the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Congress city chief Praful Gudadhe, leading the protest, said that Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi has given a diktat to conduct protests across the country for the cause. âWhat Gyanesh Kumar has done is a direct attack on democracy. You can see that the countryâs youth are out on the streets today, because they are afraid of what will happen to democracy if such voter list alterations continue,â he said, adding that their protest is against those who are trying to âendâ democracy. Chaitanya Kavy Dhruv, a CJP supporter who was detained by the cops in Delhi a couple of days ago, said that they will not be deterred by any sort of police action. âOur protest is for a just cause. CEC Kumar must resign,â he said. The rally started from Gandhi Putla at Variety Square and culminated at Samvidhan Square, where the protesters recited the Preamble out loud. âWe believe in the Constitution, and the pledge that the Preamble asks us to take. Anyone who thinks otherwise is unfit to govern the country,â AISF member Ananya said. The protesters also used a game of snakes and ladders to convey their concerns about the state of democracy. In their symbolic interpretation, the ladders represented democratic virtues and actions that advance constitutional ideals, while the snakes represented govt actions that, they argued, undermine those values and set democratic progress back. title: âWhere was this proactiveness before pollsâ: TMC, Cong question ECâs timing over voter inclusion drive
text: Kolkata: Congress and Trinamool on Tuesday questioned the Election Commission âs (EC) decision to launch a proactive campaign to ensure that no eligible voter is excluded from electoral rolls, alleging that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in Bengal was rushed through before the assembly elections, resulting in the deletion of eligible voters. Trinamool questioned why the EC had not taken similar steps before the elections and demanded accountability over alleged discrepancies in the revision process. âWhere was this proactiveness before the elections? Why was the SIR process in Bengal conducted in such a rushed and unplanned manner?â the party asked in a post on X, questioning the integrity, fairness and impartiality of the exercise. The party alleged that the SIR, conducted on the grounds of logical discrepancies, deprived eligible citizens of their voting rights. It also accused the EC of colluding with the BJP to help it win seats it otherwise could not have secured. Questioning the legitimacy of the govt formed after the elections, Trinamool said the EC must address the discrepancies and fix accountability instead of expecting citizens to accept the process without question. âNothing illegal lasts forever. Neither will the BJP government,â the party said. Meanwhile, Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh, sharing a screenshot of a press release issued by the office of the chief electoral officer (CEO), Bengal, criticised CEC Gyanesh Kumar. âAfter having delivered the assembly election to BJP in a brazenly fraudulent manner, the CEC has had this Press Note issued. There is no limit to Gyanesh Kumarâs shamelessness,â Ramesh said. According to the CEOâs office, district election officers (DEOs) across Bengal have begun a proactive campaign to identify eligible voters whose names were deleted during the SIR and facilitate their inclusion in the electoral rolls. The office said all 24 DEOs had launched the initiative in accordance with EC instructions. Special camps are being held across the state, while people with complaints have been asked to contact their respective booth-level officers (BLOs), assistant electoral registration officers (AEROs), electoral registration officers (EROs) or DEOs. âWe are committed to ensure that no eligible voter is excluded from the voter list,â the statement said. title: Bombay High Court to hear actor Imran Khanâs plea against police notice asking him to âleave Indiaâ by October 28 on Tuesday, October 27
text: Bombay High Court to hear actor Imran Khanâs plea against police notice asking him to âleave Indiaâ by October 28 on Tuesday, October 27 The Bombay High Court will hear actor Imran Khan âs petition on Tuesday against a Mumbai Police notice that asks him to leave India by October 28. The US citizen says the order, issued after a protest in Mumbai, is unfair and has no basis. Hearing fixed for Tuesday According to the PTI, the plea came up on Monday before a division bench of Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna. Imran Khanâs lawyer Venkatesh Dhond and Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, who appeared for the Centre, both asked for the matter to be taken up the next day. The bench agreed to hear it on Tuesday. Watch Imran Khan Receives October 28 Deadline to Leave India After Joining Mumbaiâs CJP Protest What led to the notice Imran Khan was held for a short time on October 10 at Mumbaiâs historic August Kranti Maidan. The gathering there was held in support of the protest in Delhi. That protest demands the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Soon after, Mumbai Police served the 43-year-old actor with a notice telling him to leave the country by October 28. Actor denies any link to organisers In his petition, Imran Khan says he did not join any gathering and has no connection with those who organised the protest. He approached the High Court on October 17. He has also received a show-cause notice from the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO), which wants to know why his Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) status should not be cancelled. Strong words against the notice Khan has described the police notice as âillegal, arbitrary, perverse and drasticâ. The petition, filed through advocate Zulfikar Memon and MZM Legal, says the notice âreflects patent non-application of mind and the arbitrary targetingâ of Imran Khan as a public figure. It also argues that the order goes too far. âNot only is the notice manifestly disproportionate, if implemented, it would reduce the very principles of natural justice that the authorities are duty-bound to uphold, to nothing but a dead letter,â the petition said. Relief sought from the court Imran Khan wants the notice quashed. He has also asked the court to put it on hold while his petition is pending and to stop the authorities from taking any coercive step against him. Legal provisions cited by police According to police, the departure order was issued under Sections 7 (2)(C) and 29 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act. These sections give the government power to restrict the movement of foreign nationals and to enforce their removal. Section 7 (2)(C) allows the government to prohibit, regulate or restrict the presence of any foreigner. It specifically lets officials order that a person âshall not remain in India or in any specified area therein.â Section 29 lets the government direct the removal of a foreign national who breaks any provision, rule or order under the Act, or in case of an adverse security report. Deportation possible if the deadline is missed Imran Khan, nephew of Bollywood superstar Aamir Khan, has appeared in several Hindi films. He has been told to leave on or before October 28. title: Voting rights being snatched away, Oppn will continue fight for citizens: Rahul
text: New Delhi: Alleging that crores of people across the country were being deprived of their voting rights through the deletion of their names from electoral rolls, Congress MP and Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi Tuesday said all Opposition parties were united on the issue and would continue fighting to protect citizensâ right. âWe have been raising this issue for a long time, but now the entire country is beginning to understand that votes are being stolen at the highest level. Poor people are being removed from electoral rolls, and their rights are being snatched awayâ¦ An attempt is being made to create a new India for a select group of billionaires, where citizens have no rights and the poor are denied their due, leaving a country that serves only the interests of billionaires,â he said, adding the Opposition would continue its campaign until CEC Gyanesh Kumar resigned or PM Narendra Modi removed him from the post. Gandhiâs remarks came while listening to residents recount their experiences at Ramlila Park in Trilokpuri, where a public hearing was organised by Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan, Jan Sarokar, Voter Adhikar Manch and National Federation of Indian Women. Volunteers from NSUI, AISA, IYC and NGOs helped residents navigate the revision process, raising awareness about the message: âJaago, jaago voter, jaago, nahi toh vote kat jayega (wake up, voters, or your names will be deleted from the electoral rolls)â. Several residents raised concerns over the names of family members missing from the rolls, while some alleged they had been wrongly marked as absent or shifted. Bijendra, a 60-year-old resident of Trilokpuriâs Indira Camp, said he was shocked when he learnt he had been marked âdeceasedâ. He said he had filled out the required form but didnât know his name had been removed. His wifeâs name, however, remains on the electoral roll. âThe officials who came asked us questions, and we answered them. We are not educated, so we thought our work was done. But now I have come to know that my name is missing from the list and that I have been declared dead. I need to get this corrected,â he said. As part of the verification exercise, volunteers visited more than 1,100 households, covering over 5,000 electors. Using digital copies of the electoral rolls downloaded from the Election Commission website, they categorised cases involving people who had not received notices, those whose submitted forms could not be traced, and voters marked as absent, deleted, shifted or deceased, said Siyaram Meena of NSUI. According to the organisers, an audit presented at the public hearing showed 2,097 of the 5,173 voters listed across the identified polling booths had been removed from the electoral rolls, accounting for 40.5% of the electorate. Of these, 1,317 voters had been visited during the verification exercise. Among the 1,236 cases that could be verified, 416 voters were found to have been wrongly removed, the organisers said. Volunteers said in several cases, BLOs had been stationed at a single location, instead of visiting individual households. âWe have asked everyone facing these issues to come to the hearing. We are first checking peopleâs house numbers and the specific problems they are facing. After that, we are issuing tokens and guiding them on how to resolve their cases. We have been helping residents for the past five days. We also visited Indira Camp in Trilokpuri,â said a volunteer. The organisers demanded mandatory public audits of draft electoral rolls at every polling booth at least three months before an election, arguing it would help identify wrongful deletions and ensure eligible voters were not excluded. title: âBarely moved for hoursâ: Commuters bear brunt of checks at GurgaonâDelhi border
text: The jam was most severe on the carriageway leading to the capital, while traffic in the opposite direction flowed relatively smoothly. GURGAON: A journey of a few kilometres towards Delhi turned into an hours long ordeal at Sirhaul border on Sunday as police checks for vehicles barred under the capitalâs new pollution curbs brought the Delhi-bound carriageway of the expressway to a near standstill. Cars, buses and two-wheelers were packed into long queues stretching from IFFCO Chowk, with commuters saying they remained stuck at the same spot for 40 minutes to over two hours, barely moving a few hundred metres. The jam was most severe on the carriageway leading to the capital, while traffic in the opposite direction flowed relatively smoothly. Buses packed with passengers were caught in the gridlock. Two-wheeler riders, usually able to weave through slow-moving traffic, found little room to manoeuvre. Some commuters eventually abandoned their cabs and walked towards Udyog Vihar and Sirhaul toll plaza. The disruption affected everyone â from those travelling to attend INDIA blocâs âChalo Delhiâ rally at Ramlila Maidan to others headed for work, hotels or home. Buses carrying rally supporters, some displaying posters of Rahul Gandhi , were also stuck in the queue. The scale of the congestion raised questions about how the checks would work on a weekday. If the enforcement drive caused such disruption on a Sunday, when regular office traffic was relatively light, Mondayâs rush could put even greater pressure on the border. Thousands of commuters use this route to enter Delhi every day. Even a brief halt at the checking points can cause queues to build up over a long stretch. Police had deployed a large force near Sirhaul, including several ACPs, traffic inspectors and crime branch teams. Multiple barricades were put up on the Gurgaon side to regulate vehicles entering Delhi. Personnel stopped motorists to check registration papers, emission standards and other documents. But commuters complained that the process was holding up even vehicles that did not fall under the restricted categories. The checks led to heated exchanges between motorists and police. Sukhbir Tanwar, Congress spokesperson in Haryana, who was stranded with supporters, was seen arguing with senior officers. He alleged that the barricades were preventing people from reaching the rally. âAs Rahul Gandhi is leading the protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi, cops have deliberately put up barricades and are not allowing us to proceed. We have been stranded for over two hours. They are trying to kill democracy,â Tanwar told TOI. He said the buses and vehicles carrying rally participants were BS-VI compliant and that organisers had taken care to ensure they met the prescribed emission standards. âPeople have come from different states to join this fight for democracy. But they have been tactfully stopped,â he alleged. The delay was no less frustrating for commuters with no connection to the rally. Ramnath Kumar Yadav, a Bhondsi resident heading to Radisson Hotel, said he was stuck for nearly an hour after crossing the Udyog Vihar underpass. His destination was only a few metres away, but a queue of buses ahead of his car left him unable to move. âMy vehicle has been stuck at one spot for over 40 minutes. I needed to take a left turn towards Radisson Hotel, which is barely a few metres away, but I cannot get through. Several buses are ahead of me and there is no one to help. I donât even know why traffic has come to a halt. This is sheer harassment,â he said. Namita, a Delhi resident who had travelled to Gurgaon for official work, said she had not expected the return journey to be so difficult. âI came here for work and had no idea that getting home would turn into such a trauma. Political rallies should be organised without putting ordinary people through this. Traffic cops should have cleared the congestion quickly, but commuters are stuck in this monster jam for no fault of theirs,â she added. Watch 15-Min Promise To Traffic Chaos: What Went Wrong With Delhiâs Barapullah Phase 3? An earthmover stationed near the toll plaza further ate into the available road space. Its operator told TOI that work was underway to install CCTV cameras at the plaza and had been continuing for the past few days. The checking drive was part of preparations for Delhiâs new restrictions, which came into force on Nov 1 to curb air pollution. Vehicles registered outside Delhi and below BS-VI emission standards are barred from entering the capital, subject to specified exemptions. Police teams were deployed at five major entry points â Aya Nagar, Gwal Pahari, Sirhaul toll, Bajghera and Kapashera â to check compliance. Satyapal Yadav, ACP (highways) in Gurgaon, said the drive began on Sunday to familiarise motorists with the restrictions and ensure compliance. âPeople were informed well in advance about Delhiâs restrictions to control air pollution. Since it was a Sunday, we began the campaign today to send a clear message that violations would not be tolerated. People should have cooperated. The checks were aimed only at ensuring effective implementation of the ban in Delhi,â he added. title: How could Congress demand resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar while sharing power with TVK govt, DMK asks
text: CHENNAI: DMK on Monday accused Congress of double standards on the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, questioning how it could demand the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi while sharing power with the TVK govt in Tamil Nadu. In a statement, the DMK cited Congress president Mallikarjun Khargeâs call for the dissolution of govts formed through what he described as a fraudulent electoral process and asked whether the Congressâs position also extended to TVK govt, which came to power in Tamil Nadu through the same electoral process. DMK hit out at the Congress for remaining silent over the detention of civil rights activists protesting against SIR in Chennai. The police action took place on the same day Congress leader Rahul Gandhi visited Chennai and met chief minister C Joseph Vijay at his Neelankarai residence. âWhile the Congress raises the banner of saving the Constitution nationally, it continues to enjoy cabinet berths in Tamil Nadu,â the statement said, accusing the party of failing to uphold the same principles when protesters were detained by the state police. Taking on Tamil Nadu Congress Committee president Manickam Tagore for questioning the absence of DMK MPs in the protest against Gyanesh Kumar at Delhi, DMK said he had no moral right to raise the question. âDMK MPs protested demanding the immediate release of students arrested by the Tamil Nadu police who protested against Gyanesh Kumar. At the same time, Rahul Gandhi was having tea with CM Vijay,â the statement said. DMK criticised the Congress for asking it to join the protest against the CEC while the partyâs state unit had remained silent over the police action against protesters in Chennai. âWe have exited the INDIA bloc after black sheep in the Congress betrayed us and acted against alliance dharma for the sake of a cabinet berth. There is no need for us to join their protests hereafter, and they have no right to compel us to do so,â DMK said in its statement, adding that the party would follow a different path from now on.
