title: 'No' to peace bond, 'yes' to INDIA bloc: Has Neha Bora outsmarted CJP leaders?
text: AISA president Neha Bora and CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke NEW DELHI: When Neha Bora recently said âAISA will not be a part of normalising the signing of peace bondsâ, she inadvertently highlighted a contrast that the Jantar Mantar 2.0 protests against SIR and "vote chori" had brought to the fore. Nehaâs refusal to sign the peace bond before a special executive magistrate and her subsequent challenge to the police move drew an obvious parallel. Did the CJP leaders - Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Sourav Das - give in to peace bond pressure easily? âPeace bonds are being weaponised to curb democratic protests. Signing such peace bonds is no less than signing away our democratic right to dissent,â the AISA national president said and claimed that she was detained within 10 minutes of protesting at Mandi House on October 16 and was told that she and other protesters were in breach of peace. âOn one side, the Constitution gives us the right to dissent. On the other hand, such peace bonds are invoked only to detain people in the name of breach of peace. Therefore, signing such peace bonds is a principally wrong decision for us. It is no less than signing away our democratic right to dissent,â Bora said defending her decision. Neha Bora on why she would not sign peace bond Bora has still not signed the bond and is awaiting copies of 6 FIRs cited as her criminal antecedents in peace-bond proceedings. This, after she insisted for all documents relied upon in the show-cause notice seeking execution of her peace bond. Now, letâs rewind to October 10. The CJPâs call for Jantar Mantar 2.0 on October 10 had, as expected, evoked great national interest and anticipation. All eyes were on Abhijeet Dipke and his associates Sourav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who had in June-July this year led a successful youth mobilisation against NEET paper leak. The CJP-led protests had ensured that Dharmendra Pradhan was forced to resign as Union education minister. After all, they were the new heroes of GenZ, who had left the politicians far behind. But ahead of October 10, the national capital saw an unprecedented clampdown. The Delhi Police closed down anything and everything that could facilitate the movement of protesters to Jantar Mantar. For the CJP leadership, the message was loud and clear - they will not get a free passage, unlike in June when they were allowed to gather and mobilise youth at Jantar Mantar for their protests against NEET paper leak. But October 10 morning started with an anticlimax. The top 3 CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das travelled together from Mumbai to Delhi and were detained from aircraft as soon as they landed in the national capital. Thousands of protesters who had responded to their calls, braved the police clampdown. They were all detained. The CJP leaders were released a day later after giving an undertaking to maintain public order. Delhi Police said a surety bond of Rs 50,000 was furnished for CJP activists Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das for maintaining peace and good behaviour for one year, following their preventive arrest on October 10. The CJP leaders made two more attempts to reclaim the streets - when Sourav Das and Ashutosh Ranka tried to reach Jantar Mantar and again when Dipke urged people to join the "Lehra Do Tiranga" march with the national flag at Central Park in Connaught Place. However, they were detained again and made to sign peace bonds to come out of detention. And while the CJP leaders failed to recreate the magic of Jantar Mantar 1.0, AISA leader Neha Bora took the centrestage. The AISA national president was detained 5 times between October 2 and October 11. However, every time she was released, she would come back to the streets and continue with her protests. During the peak of the protests, Neha Bora hogged the headlines for foxing the police. On October 11, Neha Bora announced a gathering at RK Ashram Marg Metro Station around 2:30pm as part of demonstrations heading toward central Delhi and Jantar Mantar. Heavy police deployment and barricades were set up around RK Ashram Marg to prevent demonstrators from moving toward Jantar Mantar. During the confrontation, police mistakenly chased and detained another protester whose face was partially covered, believing her to be Neha Bora. While police attention was focused at RK Ashram Marg, Neha Bora surfaced near Connaught Place (CP), breaching barricades and running alongside fellow demonstrators in a dash that went viral on social media. Little wonder then, when a user on X called Neha Bora "more talented" than CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and described her as a "complete GenZ icon", Dipke responded simply: "I agree." The X user had posted: "Maturity is realizing Neha Bora is more talented than Abhijeet Dipke. A complete GenZ icon with an absolutely ridiculous aura.â It was a comparison that manifested all along the âvote choriâ protests. Neha Bora was on the streets every time she was released from detention by the police. She was everywhere - with the CJP leadership, the social activists and also the politicians. When Rahul Gandhi chose to walk behind her during one of the protest marches of INDIA bloc, it spoke volumes about the impact she had made with her street politics. Clearly, the campaign against âvote choriâ had put the spotlight on Neha Bora, even as the CJP struggled to find their way to the centre stage of the protests. Neha Bora, along with Lok Sabha leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi, during the opposition's protest. For the CJP, it was a harsh realisation that a lot had changed between July and October. Unlike the anti-NEET paper leak protests in June-July, the Congress-led INDIA bloc this time around were already on the streets demanding resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Interestingly, while the INDIA blocâs original protest schedule had only one announced street protest on October 6, the group returned back to the streets four days in a row till October 9, which was a day before the announced CJP protest. The CJP and the Congress had stayed away from each other during the anti-NEET protests. After Jantar Mantar 1.0 was over, the 'cockroaches' carried out their own campaigns in different states, while the Congress shifted focus to protests against SIR and CEC Gyanesh Kumar. So when CJP announced support for INDIA blocâs November 1 rally, it set tongues wagging about their political ambitions. With CJPâs Jantar Mantar 2.0 not shaping out as they would have hoped, perhaps its leadership should take a leaf out of Saurav Dasâs advice on X to a Congress âsoldierâ who had questioned why youth Congress and NSUI activists were being detained as soon as they hit the streets and cockroaches were allowed to roam free. Responding to him, CJP co-founder Saurav Das had then said: âif u guys r detained immediately, then u must rethink ur strategy. donât blame others for ur failures.â The context of that remark was different and CJPâs Jantar Mantar 2.0 campaign was in no way a failure, but Sourav's take on ârethinking strategyâ perhaps holds true for the cockroaches at present. title: 'Lady hiding in Dehradun': Who was Rahul Gandhi referring to at INDIA bloc presser?
text: Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge, party leaders Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, KC Venugopal, and other leaders of the INDIA bloc address a joint press conference, in New Delhi. (PTI Photo) NEW DELHI: âIt is our commitment to you that the people who have done this, Mr. Modi, Mr. Shah, Mr. Gyanesh Kumar, the lady who's hiding right now in Dehradun, and others are going to be brought to justice," Rahul Gandhi said announcing a united INDIA bloc's resolve to continue its agitation against alleged SIR irregularities. A day after the INDIA bloc's high-voltage protest march against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral irregularities, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi hosted a high tea for opposition leaders at his residence. Following the meeting, INDIA bloc leaders addressed a press conference. Watch 'Unable To...': CJI Surya Kant Responds To INDIA Bloc Letter Amid SIR Row | Rahul Gandhiâs SC March "Yesterday, you saw an expression not of the political party standing here, but an expression of the people of India...We would like to thank the people of Delhi, the people of India, who stood with us against what is being done. This is not about us. This is about the people of India," Rahul said. But then who was the 'lady hiding right now in Dehradun' whom the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha was referring to in his statement? Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders have been relentless in their attacks on the Prime Minister and the Union home minister, but it was his reference to a 'lady hiding in Dehradun' that added an element of mystery to the press conference. Was the Congress leader referring to Seema Khanna, the Election Commission's Director General (IT), whose name has figured in opposition allegations of 'vote theft'? There is no confirmation that Khanna is the woman Rahul was referring to. The Congress leader did not identify her, and there is no independently verified information linking her to Dehradun. However, her name has repeatedly surfaced in allegations raised by opposition leaders against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Why is Seema Khanna's name in the controversy? Khanna's name came into focus following a report by The Indian Express, which said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Among the concerns raised was the growing centralisation of control over electoral-roll software and restrictions on the powers of Electoral Registration Officers (EROs), who are legally responsible for maintaining voter lists. The controversy centred on the Election Commission's digital systems, including ERONet and ECINet, which are used to manage electoral rolls and election-related services. ECINet is a unified digital platform developed by the Election Commission to streamline electoral processes and improve transparency and accessibility. The investigation raised questions about whether local election officials had adequate access to make corrections, restore voters' names and exercise their statutory powers, or whether some of these functions had become concentrated within the Commission's IT department headed by Khanna. Rahul Gandhi did not name Seema Khanna, but AICC media coordinator Harmeet Kaur appeared to draw a connection between his remark and the EC official in a post on X. "Where is Seema Khanna? Is she hiding in Dehradun? And who is shielding her? Remember EC data still under her control! Who is protecting her, and what are they trying to hide?" Kaur wrote, sharing a video of Rahul's remarks at the press conference. Last month, Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra filed a police complaint against CEC Gyanesh Kumar at Delhi's Parliament Street Police Station, alleging procedural violations, unilateral decision-making and manipulation of electoral rolls. Speaking to ANI, Moitra directly named Khanna while accusing the Election Commission of manipulating voter lists through its software. "Very important things like the crores of new voters were not being allowed to come on the list because of the addition of a new question on Form 6, the new voters list. And we now find that the two other election commissioners had said this is completely illegal; still, the question linking parentage was put in," Mahua Moitra had said. "We find how the EROs and the BLOs and the ground-level officials were not kept in the loop and denied access to the software, and Seema Khanna, who was DGIT, along with Gyanesh Kumar, played with the software from the back end to manipulate voter lists while keeping EROs and block-level officials in the dark. This is a very serious charge," she alleged. The protesters were part of a group of around 250 to 300 people who joined a nationwide agitation seeking the CECâs resignation. Demonstrators gathered at Ashok Stambh before starting a march through key city roads. Police moved in soon after the march began and detained several participants. Despite the action, the protest continued through Meher Signal, MG Road and Sangli Bank Signal before heading towards CBS Road. Senior police officers said the 26 were detained under sections 68 and 69 of the Maharashtra Police Act. The protesters carried placards and banners demanding the scrapping of the SIR process, restoration of voting through ballot papers and the resignation of the CEC. They also displayed posters critical of govt. Police said the situation remained under control and no untoward incident was reported during the march. title: Mahatma Gandhiâs great-grandson, Tushar Gandhi detained in Mumbai
text: Activist Tushar Gandhi was taken into custody by Mumbai police just before a planned demonstration at August Kranti Maidan MUMBAI: Mumbai Police on Saturday detained activist Tushar Gandhi and others ahead of a proposed demonstration at August Kranti Maidan in solidarity with the Cockroach Janta Partyâs ( CJP ) protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Delhiâs Jantar Mantar. Tushar Gandhi, the great-grandson of Mahatma Gandhi and head of the organisation âHum Bharat Ke Logâ, was picked up from Bandra and taken to DN Nagar police station, an official said. Gandhi had shared a poster on X urging citizens to join a protest gathering at August Kranti Maidan at 3.30pm. Activist Feeroz Mithiborwala was also taken into custody from his residence and shifted to the MIDC police station, officials said. The detentions came ahead of the proposed demonstration, which was organised in solidarity with the CJPâs planned mobilisation at Jantar Mantar against alleged irregularities in the electoral process. Authorities said August Kranti Maidan is not a designated protest site under a Bombay High Court order. Police took preventive action to maintain law and order ahead of the proposed demonstration. title: Protesters demand CECâs resignation, police block march in Guwahati
text: Police stop protesters from taking out a procession from the Chachal site in Guwahati Guwahati: Tension prevailed at the Chachal protest site here on Saturday as nearly 300 people gathered for a satyagraha demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the withdrawal of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The protest was organised by political parties, civil society groups and student and youth organisations in solidarity with a student-led protest in New Delhi. Police stopped the protesters from taking out a procession from the site. The protest witnessed strong criticism of the BJP-led govt, with speakers accusing it of undermining democratic institutions and creating an âundeclared emergency-like situationâ in the country. A large contingent of security personnel was deployed at the site from the morning to prevent any escalation. The meeting, conducted by youth activists Subrat Talukdar and Krishna Gogoi, called for the satyagraha to continue until the CEC resigns. Assam Jatiya Parishad president Lurinjyoti Gogoi, Congress leaders Ripun Bora and Meera Borthakur, CPI(ML) Liberation state general secretary Bibek Das, writer Junu Bora, academic Prof. Apurba Kumar Baruah, Assam Nagrik Sanmilanâs Paresh Malakar, and youth leaders â Utpala Das, Ananya Saikia, Bidisha Barman, Birinchi Bora â and representatives of student and youth organisations addressed the gathering. âThe way the govt is using independent democratic institutions to deprive citizens of their rights, including their voting rights, has created a grave crisis for the entire democratic system. The right to vote is the cornerstone of our democracy and our greatest strength,â Lurinjyoti said. Intellectual Hiren Gohain, who could not attend the programme due to illness, addressed the protesters on the phone. In a media release, the organisers alleged that the Election Commission , particularly CEC Kumar, had facilitated electoral victories for BJP through various manipulations. They cited the SIR exercise as an example, claiming it had curtailed the voting rights of 13 crore citizens. âIt has already been proven how the Election Commission, especially chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, has been helping BJP win elections through various manipulations. A glaring example of this is the truncation of the voting rights of 13 crore citizens through the SIR. If these manipulations continue, BJP will keep winning elections forever,â the organisers said. title: Revanth accuses Modi Govt of getting 20 cr votes deleted
text: Hyderabad: Chief minister A Revanth Reddy on Monday alleged that Narendra Modi govt at the Centre was afraid of losing the next election and had given chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar the task of removing 20 crore anti-Modi and anti-BJP votes via the special intensive revision (SIR). The NDA govt led by Modi is trying to divide the country into two classes of people â one who were rich and had voting rights, and another who were poor and included adivasis, Dalits, Girijans and minorities without voting rights, he alleged. âThere is a danger of this second category of people who are not in favour of Modi and BJP being reduced to second-class citizens. The BJP is snatching their votes with the intention of winning the next election and remaining in power. The trio of Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and CEC Gyanesh Kumar is indulging in âvote chori âunder the guise of SIR,â Revanth alleged, addressing reporters at Telangana Bhavan in New Delhi. Revanth, along with TPCC president Mahesh Kumar Goud, ministers, MPs, MLCs, MLAs, Congress district presidents and corporation chairpersons from Telangana, also participated in a march from Barakhamba to Supreme Court , along with Rahul Gandhi and other AICC and INDIA alliance leaders, demanding Gyanesh Kumarâs resignation. âTo ensure that Dalit, adivasi, minorities and downtrodden citizens continue to have voting rights, as given by B R Ambedkar in the Constitution, Rahul Gandhi is leading another freedom movement,â Revanth said. BJP has won elections in the states where it could not have won without the SIR, he alleged. BJP first stoked discord between religions and regions. Then it started misusing CBI, IT, ED, Narcotics bureau. Then it realised it would be difficult to win the next election even by misusing all these institutions and changed the selection committee member to appoint the chief election commissioner. BJP govt removed the Chief Justice of India and brought in the Union home minister to the selection committee. âNow, it is misusing ECI,â he alleged. How can the number of voters decrease when the population is increasing, Revanth asked and pointed out that there were 81 crore voters in 2014, 91 crore in 2019, and 97 crore in 2024. Over 13 crore votes had already been deleted. If the population is increasing and has crossed 140 crore, then the number of voters should have crossed 100 crore, he said. Revanth alleged that it was being used to identify and delete anti-BJP votes. He expressed strong indignation, stating that the votes of young people who post against PM Modi on social media were also being removed. title: âSpare India from anarchyâ: Over 400 Indian-origin students, academics condemn anti-EC protests
text: NEW DELHI: More than 400 Indian-origin students, researchers and alumni from universities in 27 countries have issued a joint statement condemning the ongoing protests against the Election Commission of India (ECI), describing them as a âplan to sow seeds of doubt in Indiaâs democracyâ. Titled âSpare India from Anarchyâ, the statement criticises the protests against the poll body. "An unconscionable and devious plan of sowing seeds of doubt in Indian democracy has been hatched by weaponising sub judice matters, which is then amplified on the streets by leaning on anarchist forces, which have historically and philosophically never believed in constitutional form of governance. All in the name of saving democracy," the statement said. Watch EC Makes 4 Changes To SSR Amid Anti-CEC Protests; Congress Says âToo Little, Too Lateâ "We remain amazed at the irony of all. But more importantly, as informed people who have stakes in the future of this country and travel the world identifying as 'Indians,' we are deeply anguished at this state of affairs," it added. The signatories highlighted the resilience of Indian democracy and the role of constitutional institutions, stating: "In the seven decades since independence, Indian democracy has proved its resilience repeatedly. Institutions have flourished, checks and balances have functioned admirably, and peaceful transition of power has remained an enduring hallmark." They lamented that "a frenzy of election denial, relentless questioning of constitutional institutions, and a preference for 'street over Sansad'" had gripped certain quarters. "Unfavourable election outcomes have led to questions of procedural integrity. Adverse judgements have provoked unfortunate commentary on judicial independence. Even the most apolitical institution in the country -- the armed forces -- has been gratuitously and unjustly entangled in partisan discourse," the statement read. While acknowledging that dissent was essential to democracy, the signatories said they refused to remain "silent spectators to the subversion of democratic apparatus in its guise". They urged social and political forces to resolve differences through "debate, discussion, dialogue and dissent" within constitutional institutions. The signatories are based in or have studied at universities across 27 countries, including the US, the UK, Canada, Australia, Germany, France, Japan and Singapore. Their academic affiliations include the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, the universities of Oxford and Cambridge, Harvard University, Stanford University and the London School of Economics, among others. The statement clarified that these affiliations did not imply endorsement by the respective universities. Why is India witnessing anti-EC protests The protests come amid opposition partiesâ allegations of irregularities in elections and questions over the integrity of electoral processes. Last month, The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions they claimed were taken without their knowledge, including those related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. title: Bombay HC to hear actor Imran Khanâs plea on Oct 26, two days before FRRO deadline
text: Imran Khan Mumbai: Bombay HC on Monday said it will on Oct 26 hear actor and US national Imran Khan âs petition against a notice to leave India following an anti-CEC stir, two days before the deadline set by the Foreigners Regional Registration Officer (FRRO), Mumbai. The Chief Justice-led bench asked the actor to also make the state a party. Senior counsel Venkatesh Dhond for Khan (43) mentioned the matter for urgent hearing. He said the actor has been living in India since the age of 2 and has been âasked to leave without notice, without any hearing, without reasonsâ. He said the petition states that Khan has no criminal antecedents. Watch Tiger Shroff Firing Case: Police Seize Bike, Probe Salman Khan Threat Audio; Fadnavis Reacts Dhond sought a hearing this week. Additional solicitor general Anil Singh for the Centre and FRRO said it could be heard on Oct 26. Dhond said since the actor has been asked to leave by Oct 28, it would be cutting it too close. Singh, however, said, âWe will come prepared to argue the matter.â Khan was issued the notice by FRRO on Oct 14 following his brief detention from the site of a protest held in the city on Oct 10 against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The HC bench asked if all parties had been served a copy of the petition. Dhond said it had been. Singh said he had received a copy of the petition â10 minutes agoâ. The actor had filed the petition on Saturday challenging the notice as âarbitrary, unreasoned and wholly misconceivedââ and against principles of natural justice. The plea said the FRRO notice is based on âpurported contravention of uncited provisions of Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, and rules and ordersâ under it. The petition said merely reproducing the words of a statutory provision mechanically is not sufficient in law and cannot be countenanced. It said the actor has been given the expulsion order solely because an FIR has been registered, which is at the stage of investigation. It said the offences alleged in the FIR are all bailable and none carries punishment exceeding two years in jail. It said no chargesheet has been filed yet, no court has taken cognisance, and no charge has been framed. âEven if a chargesheet were to be filed, the court may decline to take cognisance. If it takes cognisance, the petitioner may be discharged. If charges are framed, he may be acquitted. To expel the petitioner at the very threshold of that process is to visit the ultimate consequence upon a mere allegation and to condemn him, in effect, on the mere recording by police of an intimation of the commission of an offence,â it said. title: Special summary revision of poll roll in 17 states
text: Only for voter list updation; paused post-2024 NEW DELHI: Election Commission Thursday ordered special summary revision (SSR) of electoral rolls in 17 states/Union territories (UT) â including the five states due for assembly elections early next year â with reference to Jan 1, 2027 as the qualifying date. This is the first SSR exercise â which, unlike special intensive revision (SIR) that prepares electoral roll de novo, is a mere updation of the roll with no house-to-house visits by booth-level officers (BLOs) â to be undertaken after it was paused post-2024, on account of SIR that started with Bihar in June 2025 and has since covered 31 states/UTs in back-to-back phases. The third phase of SIR, covering 19 states/UTs, is still underway, with only a few states completed. title: Missing pages, Rs 200 fee shortfall: SC flags 14 defects in INDIA bloc plea against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
text: SC flags over 10 defects in Rahul's plea against CEC Gyanesh Kumar NEW DELHI: Supreme Court registry Monday flagged 14 defects in a petition filed by the Rahul Gandhi-led INDIA bloc against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged large-scale voter deletions and irregularities in the special intensive revision of electoral rolls. The registry asked the lawyer who filed the petition to submit a clear copy of the identity card of Congress chief and leader of opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge , one of the co-petitioners, news agency PTI reported. Watch 14 Defects: Supreme Court Flags Rahul Gandhiâs Plea Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, EC | INDIA Bloc The registry also flagged illegible or missing pages in the petition. It further pointed out a shortfall of Rs 220 in the court fee. Meanwhile, Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut responded to the Supreme Court registry flagging defects in the opposition bloc's petition, saying the INDIA bloc remained determined to hold the constitutional body accountable. Speaking to news agency ANI about the technical discrepancies in the petition, Raut said, "The petition that has been filed mentions that the fee is short by Rs 220, there are several errors, and there are facts about 14 documents mentioned in it. Well, it is possible. We have individual petitions in the names of Rahul Ji, Mallikarjun Kharge Ji, and all other India Bloc leaders. There might be some errors in it, which we will now rectify and repair. " Confirming his participation in the legal challenge, Raut said, "Definitely, I am a petitioner. All the parties that were involved in yesterday's protest are all petitioners." On Monday, Rahul and several other opposition leaders marched to the Supreme Court to file the petition. title: âError 404: Voter name not foundâ: Students, citizens of Bengaluru demand Gyanesh Kumarâs resignation
text: Hundreds of Bengalureans gathered at Freedom Park Sunday to oppose SIR and condemn the detention of activists in the country Bengaluru: âAsking questions isnât anarchy. Abusing power is.â These were the words on a placard held aloft at Freedom Park Sunday, as hundreds of citizens and students gathered to oppose the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, demand chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumarâs resignation and condemn the detention of protesters a day earlier. The demonstration, organised by the Karnataka state committee of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), saw at least 300 participants holding banners criticising the Election Commission of India (ECI) and the Centre. Others carried placards with messages such as âSay no to SIR! Gyanesh Kumar must go!â and âWhen? Where? Accountability where?â Protesters also shared personal experiences of SIR, arguing that concerns over electoral rolls and accountability could not be silenced through detentions. Another placard read, âError 404: Voter name not found!â, reflecting concerns over discrepancies in voter lists. While anti-SIR protests have largely centred on the National Capital Region, organisers said citizens should be able to participate from wherever they live, without having to travel to Delhi. âWherever we stay, we should make our voice heard. The idea is simple. I wanted to be at Jantar Mantar but couldnât. Hence, we demand accountability from Bengaluru,â said Mohammad Affan, a CJP member. For some protesters, the demands extended beyond the CECâs resignation. Bhavana, CJPâs south zone coordinator, said changes to the selection process for election commissioners and the conduct of SIR were central concerns. âPeople are frustrated. I wasnât personally affected by SIR, but my mother was because her surname changed after marriage. We arenât just asking for Gyaneshâs resignation. It is mostly about the law which was passed, removing the Chief Justice of India from the selection panel of ECI. We want SIR to be revoked, and we donât want these types of systemic failures anymore,â she said. The gathering also saw members of student organisations, including the All India Studentsâ Association (AISA). Its members had attempted to march from Freedom Park towards the ECI office on Saturday but were detained by police. Aditi S, one of those detained and later released, said she was injured during the incident. She also questioned the Congress-led Karnataka govtâs position on the right to protest. âWe started the march from Freedom Park and were all detained... Police were brutally pulling our legs. I did get injured in the process. There were people even in civil clothing handling the protesters,â she said. Drawing a comparison with protests in Delhi, she added: âIn Delhi, we see Rahul Gandhi himself breaking the barricades, but when it happens in states ruled by them (Congress), we get detained.â Police said on Saturday that AISA members were detained for allegedly breaching the designated protest site when they tried to march from Freedom Park towards the ECI office. Pratik Khedkar, another protester, said the demand for CECâs resignation was straightforward. âPeople arenât happy with a govt official; they just want him to resign. Thereâs nothing too big here. This govt especially fears any form of protest,â he said. Kâtaka citizens on way to Delhi held, freed The dayâs gathering was partly prompted by the detention of members travelling from Karnataka to Delhi, said Rahul Philip, CJPâs south zone coordinator. âAs per the verified information we got, at least two CJP members from Karnataka were detained midway to Delhi. Some were stopped when they reached Delhi and were taken to undisclosed locations. They got released today, but in an entirely different, unknown location,â he said. The organisers concluded the Freedom Park demonstration by singing the national anthem and said protests would continue until their demands were met. No detentions were reported on Sunday. title: Lakhs of electors at risk of being disenfranchised during SIR: TPCC chief
text: Hyderabad: Telangana Congress president B Mahesh Kumar Goud on Monday alleged that lakhs of voter names are under the threat of being removed from the electoral rolls in the state under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of votersâ list. Mahesh Kumar Goud said the Congress would write to civil society organisations, NGOs and caste-based associations in Telangana, urging them to help safeguard the voting rights of people whose names are under threat of being excluded or have been excluded from the electoral rolls. Watch âWould See Who Modified Form 6â: Supreme Court Refuses To Suspend CEC Gyanesh Kumar He spoke to media persons in New Delhi after attending a key meeting convened by the AICC, chaired by AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge , Rahul Gandhi and AICC general secretary K C Venugopal. The meeting discussed the Congressâ concerns over the electoral-roll revision process and the course of action to be adopted in the coming weeks, and demanded the resignation of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. Mahesh Kumar Goud said the meeting decided to intensify protests over the alleged irregularities in the SIR process for the next two months. He said rallies and demonstrations would be organised against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and demanded his resignation. The TPCC chief alleged that the Election Commission was functioning under pressure from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah. âRahul Gandhi has stressed that every eligible citizen must retain the right to vote. The TPCC will organise protests and rallies from the village level to the state level on Oct 6 and 7. âA protest would be held in front of Lok Bhavan in Hyderabad on Oct 8,â he said. Telangana CEO C Sudharshan Reddy on Thursday said that about 54 lakh of the 92 lakh voters issued notices during the SIR process had been included in the electoral rolls. This process will continue till Nov 5. The collection of documents from the remaining nearly 40 lakh will be completed, and they will be brought into the main rolls, except those who have migrated or died, he said. Meanwhile, the Telangana Congress Seva Dal held a satyagraha at Gandhi Bhavan on Monday to safeguard democracy, demanding the immediate resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar. TPCC Seva Dal state president Middela Jitender alleged that the Election Commission was actually removing votes and termed the SIR exercise as âSystematic Identification and Removalâ of votersâ names. âThis is a premeditated attack on the democratic system. CEC Gyanesh Kumar, who is expected to act impartially, is undermining the spirit of the Constitution by siding with the BJP govt at the Centre,â he alleged. Jitender and other leaders who spoke at the satyagraha said they would intensify their agitation across the state against the anti-people policies of the BJP govt at the Centre. title: AISA workers detained during protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar in Delhi
text: Workers of the All India Students' Association detained NEW DELHI: Workers of the All India Students' Association (AISA) were detained by Delhi Police while protesting against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar near RK Puram on Sunday, as the protest called by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) entered its second day amid heavy security deployment across the capital. Over 100 protesters were detained as they raised slogans and attempted to march towards Jantar Mantar from different parts of Delhi. Several were seen being dragged into police buses. Watch Neha Bora Detained: Protesters Surround Police Bus, Demand AISA Presidentâs Release Members of several student organisations, including the Students' Federation of India (SFI), AISA and Krantikari Yuva Sangathan (KYS), along with CJP supporters, were detained during the protests. CPI(M) Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas was also among those detained, police sources said. Visuals showed protesters marching through Connaught Place's Inner Circle and near Rajiv Chowk, raising slogans demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The demonstrators could be heard shouting, "Gyanesh Kumar isteefa do, isteefa do". Security personnel were seen moving towards the protesters and attempting to disperse them. Several demonstrators resisted as police personnel held them by their arms and pulled them towards waiting buses. Some protesters were seen being dragged along the road, while others continued raising slogans as they were taken into custody. Protesters marching from RK Ashram Marg metro station were also detained as police maintained a heavy presence at several locations to prevent demonstrators from reaching Jantar Mantar. More than 40 protesters were detained near RK Ashram Marg, police sources said, adding that the total number of detainees across the city could reach around 100 by the afternoon. The SFI alleged that hundreds of its activists had been detained and taken to Surajmal Stadium in Nangloi. In a statement, the organisation said its All India President Adarsh M Saji, Delhi State Secretary Sooraj Elamon, Central Executive Committee member Abhijith Manilal and several other members were detained during the protest. The SFI alleged that its leaders were assaulted inside cage-like police vans. It also claimed that Brittas was attacked by Delhi Police personnel and later left by the roadside in an injured condition. The organisation further alleged that Father Biju Xavier, the vicar of Sacred Heart Church in Delhi, was "arrested" while recording a video of alleged police violence on his mobile phone. AISA president Neha Bora, who had earlier called for a demonstration at RK Ashram Marg at 2.30 pm, was detained along with other protesters near Vijay Chowk. Visuals showed Bora raising slogans alongside other members of the organisation as security personnel moved towards them. She and the other demonstrators were seen running as police personnel attempted to stop them before detaining them. The CJP said several of its protesters had been detained near Connaught Place metro station and Gurdwara Bangla Sahib. Videos shared by the organisation showed protesters attempting to form human chains as police personnel moved in to detain them. The organisation alleged that doctors and other demonstrators protesting peacefully near Gurdwara Bangla Sahib were also taken into custody. In another development, videos circulating on social media showed KYS members staging a protest on boats near Nigambodh Ghat. Holding posters, they raised slogans demanding the resignation of the chief election commissioner. Members of the organisation were also seen demonstrating near Connaught Place. The detentions came amid extensive security arrangements across the capital, with police personnel deployed at several locations to prevent protesters from reaching Jantar Mantar. The CJP had announced another demonstration at the protest site at 10 am on Sunday after police prevented its supporters from gathering there on Saturday. More than 30,000 police and paramilitary personnel have been deployed across Delhi as part of the security arrangements. On Saturday, CJP leaders, including Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, were detained amid a major security clampdown. More than 7,000 protesters were detained at multiple locations as police prevented them from reaching Jantar Mantar. Several opposition leaders, including former chief ministers Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan and Manik Sarkar, were also detained while attempting to join the protest. The CJP and opposition parties have been demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the functioning of the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. text: Dipke urged the CEC to resign, claiming that election results in the country had become "predetermined" and that participation in such polls had therefore become meaningless. PUNE: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activist Abhijeet Dipke alleged that the BJP is winning in states where it could not secure victories even during the peak of the "Modi wave", attributing the outcome to alleged institutional manipulation under chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. "I feel that until Gyanesh Kumar resigns and ensures free and fair elections, there is no point in participating in such polls, because the winner is already predetermined," he said. Dipke made the remarks during his visit to Pune to express solidarity with students protesting against the Maharashtra government over alleged irregularities in Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) examinations and recruitment backlogs. He linked the issue surrounding the polls to alleged administrative failures under the ruling dispensation and claimed that public trust in both competitive examinations and electoral processes had collapsed. Seeking the resignation of the MPSC Chairman, Dipke said, "I have come here to meet protesting students. Their future is in question because there are continuous cases of paper leaks. text: Congress workers during their march on Tuesday Ranchi: Congress workers briefly clashed with the police on Tuesday during their protest outside the office of state chief electoral officer (CEO) in Dhurwa seeking the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. title: Admin warns against unauthorised protests
text: Security personnel stand guard in Patna on Saturday Patna : Security was stepped up across Patna on Saturday amid concerns over demonstrations linked to the Cockroach Janata Partyâs protest in Delhi against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and the SIR issue. The district administration also warned of legal action against protests held outside the designated site at Gardanibagh without prior permission. Rapid Action Force personnel were deployed at Gandhi Maidan, while CRPF and Bihar Police personnel were positioned near J P Golambar. Iron barricades were erected at Dakbungalow Square, with additional security along key roads and public spaces to prevent unauthorised gatherings and traffic disruption. The alert came as the All India Democratic Studentsâ Organization (AIDSO) staged a demonstration near Patna College, demanding the CECâs resignation. Police detained three student members before the protest began: state president Vijay Kumar, state secretary Pawan Kumar and organisation member Raj. They questioned the action, saying they had planned a peaceful demonstration and were exercising their democratic right to protest. In a communique, the district administration said demonstrations at locations other than Gardanibagh were causing traffic congestion and inconvenience. Patna district magistrate (DM) Kundan Kumar and SSP said smooth traffic movement, public convenience and law and order were priorities. The administration said unauthorised protests could disrupt schools, colleges, hospitals, courts and govt offices, besides obstructing ambulances and other emergency services. It urged organisations to hold peaceful demonstrations only at the designated site and warned that violations would invite legal action. Meanwhile, the protests disrupted rail services between Bihar and Delhi, inconveniencing passengers. The affected Patna-Delhi services were restored on Saturday. Central range inspector general (IG) Jitendra Rana said police were primarily focused on security for Durga Puja , which begins on Sunday. âCCTV surveillance and regular patrolling are being arranged to manage crowds and prevent crime,â he said. text: TNCC senior leaders and cadres stage a demonstration in Chennai on Thursday, protesting the arrest of Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders and MPs in Delhi. The protesters were detained while marching to the Election Commission demanding the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of voter-roll manipulation. Chennai: Tamil Nadu Congress Committee on Thursday held a protest in Chennai condemning the arrest of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and INDIA bloc MPs for organising an agitation demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Congress said INDIA bloc would organise protest meetings across Tamil Nadu on Oct 13 and 14 against the CEC. At the protest on Anna Salai in Chennai, TNCC functionaries raised slogans against Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah , accusing BJP-led Union govt of using force to suppress the Opposition. Congress functionaries burnt an effigy and posters carrying images of Modi, Shah and Kumar, causing temporary traffic congestion in the area. The protesters demanded Kumarâs immediate removal, alleging the deletion of 13 crore names from the electoral rolls through SIR across the country was an âunlawful act.â Former TNCC president Thirunavukkarasar said Congress and its allies would continue their agitation until Kumar was removed or resigned. He said Opposition parties were considering measures like approaching Supreme Court seeking Kumarâs removal and moving a resolution in the parliament in this regard when the parliament meets. âCongress will not rest until Gyanesh Kumar is removed from office. Rahul Gandhi has made it clear that the agitation will continue until he is removed,â Thirunavukkarasar said. TN Congress legislature party leader Tharahai Cuthbert, senior leader Peter Alphonse and several other functionaries attended the demo, while ministers Rajesh Kumar and P Viswanathan did not turn up for the demo.
